# Arbitrica articles (full text)

> Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that gets you what you are buying at the lowest price on Earth. It lives in your browser and shows up at the checkout when you are about to pay, searches the same hotel, product or event tickets from 195 countries, validates that the item is identical and that the price includes all taxes and fees, and then gets it for you at that price.

Key facts:
- Arbitrica searches from 195 countries. Different countries get access to different inventory, sales channels, local rates and promotions, so the same item can be cheaper when searched from another country.
- Two mechanisms: geographic arbitrage (the same item searched from 195 countries) and time arbitrage (live arbitrage at checkout, and multiple-time arbitrage that repeats the search after purchase until the cancellation or return window ends).
- Categories: hotels (with Agent Butler), online shopping such as Amazon, and event tickets; the same mechanisms apply to flights, car rental, subscriptions, pre-orders and more.
- Arbitrica serves individuals and companies: teams travelling to trade shows and conferences, operations managers and travel managers.
- Typical outcome: the same item is often 5-30% cheaper elsewhere; research demonstrated an average of $47 per hotel booking (up to $3,000 a year), $34 per online purchase (up to $3,000 a year) and $107 per event ticket purchase (up to $1,500 a year). Real example: a hotel offered at $1,527.39 on Booking was found for $1,180.27, earning the traveler $347.12 (23%).

# AI hotel booking: what AI agents actually do for price

AI assistants are good at picking a hotel. Here is what it takes for one to find the lowest price for that hotel, and prove it before you pay.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/ai-hotel-booking.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: AI agents

## Key takeaways

- Most AI travel assistants are built to choose a hotel, not to find the lowest price for it.
- A typical assistant searches from your own country, so it sees the same prices you would.
- The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when searched from another country.
- Agent Butler, Arbitrica's in-chat agent for hotels, searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout and prepares the booking for you to review and pay.
- A good AI agent shows the final total, confirms the hotel is identical and never pays without your approval.

AI hotel booking has gone from a novelty to something many travelers try at least once. You describe the trip in a sentence, an assistant suggests a few hotels, and sometimes it walks you most of the way to a confirmed reservation. What is less clear is whether any of this gets you a better price. Most AI tools are very good at finding a hotel you will like. Far fewer are built to find the lowest price for that hotel.

This guide looks at what AI booking agents actually do today, where they help with price and where they do not, and how Arbitrica, a personal AI agent built around price, works at the moment you are about to pay, including Agent Butler, its in-chat agent for hotels.

## What "AI hotel booking" means in practice

The phrase covers three quite different kinds of tools, and it helps to keep them apart.

- **Chat assistants.** General AI chatbots that plan trips, suggest neighborhoods, summarize reviews and recommend hotels. Some can pull live availability through partner integrations.

- **AI features inside booking sites.** Search boxes that accept plain language ("quiet hotel near the old town with a pool, under $250 a night") and filters that understand what you mean.

- **Personal AI agents that act for you.** Agents, often living in your browser, that take steps on your behalf: running searches, checking details and preparing a booking. This is where the term "autonomous hotel booking AI" usually points.

The first two are mostly about choice. The third can be about price, depending on what the agent is designed to do.

## What AI booking agents do well today

Current AI tools are strong at tasks that used to take an evening of open tabs:

- Turning a vague request into a short list of hotels that match it.

- Reading hundreds of reviews and telling you what guests keep mentioning, such as street noise, slow elevators or a great breakfast.

- Checking practical details: distance to a venue, airport transfer options, whether parking is on site.

- Building an itinerary around the hotel you pick.

Where most of them stop is the final step. A sensible AI agent does not pay for you without asking, and the good ones are built so that you always review the booking and confirm the payment yourself. That is a design choice worth looking for, not a weakness.

## Where AI helps with hotel prices, and where it does not

Here is the gap. A typical AI travel assistant searches the way you would: from your own country, on one site or a handful of sites. It can tell you that Hotel A is cheaper than Hotel B. It usually cannot tell you that Hotel A itself is cheaper when searched from somewhere else.

That second question matters because hotel prices are not one number. Different countries get access to different inventory, distribution channels, local rates and promotions, so searching the same hotel from another country can open up prices you cannot get from your own country. The mechanics are covered in [what geographic price arbitrage is](https://arbitrica.com/blog/what-is-geographic-price-arbitrage.html) and in the [guide to hidden hotel prices](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hidden-hotel-prices-guide.html).

| Question | Typical AI travel assistant | Personal AI agent (Arbitrica) |

| What is it? | Chatbot or booking-site feature | Personal AI agent (lives in your browser) |

| Which hotel suits my trip? | Strong | Not its job; you choose the hotel |

| Is this hotel cheaper from another seller? | Sometimes, from your own country | Searches the same hotel from 195 countries |

| Is the lower price really the same hotel? | Rarely checked | Validates the identical hotel |

| Does the price include taxes and fees? | Varies | Validates the total, taxes and fees included |

| Who pays? | You | You, after reviewing what the agent prepared |

The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper elsewhere. In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, with a typical gap of 20-40%. That spread is why a price-focused agent behaves differently from a planning assistant.

## How Agent Butler works at checkout

Agent Butler is Arbitrica's in-chat agent for hotels. Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser, so it is there at the point that matters: the checkout page, just before you pay. You pick the hotel and dates as you normally would, on whatever site you like. Then:

- **It reads what you are buying**The hotel, dates, guests and the total you are about to pay.

- **It searches the same hotel from 195 countries**This is live arbitrage: the search happens in real time, while you are at checkout. No one can do this by hand, since checking 195 countries one at a time through a VPN is not realistic.

- **It validates the result**Arbitrica checks that the lower price is for the identical hotel, that it includes all taxes and fees, and that the price will not suddenly change when you go to pay.

- **It prepares everything**The booking at the lowest price on Earth is set up for you, at a different seller from the one you started on.

- **You review and pay**Nothing is paid without you. If the lower price does not suit you, you keep the booking you started with.

> Chart: At checkout Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries, checks it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price.

A real example: a user was offered $1,527.39 for a stay on Booking.com. Arbitrica found the identical hotel for $1,180.27, which earned that user $347.12, or 23%. Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

> Chart: A real booking: offered at $1,527.39, found for $1,180.27 for the identical hotel. Arbitrica earned the user $347.12 (23%).

Arbitrica also serves companies: teams traveling to trade shows and conferences, and the operations and travel managers who book for them. The full flow is on the [how it works](https://arbitrica.com/how-it-works.html) page.

## What happens after you book: time arbitrage

Prices keep moving after you pay. The second family of mechanisms Arbitrica developed is time arbitrage. Live arbitrage is the search at checkout. Multiple-time arbitrage repeats the search after you book, for as long as your free cancellation window is open. When it finds the identical hotel at a lower total, Arbitrica's approach is to prepare a new booking at that price and cancel the original only once the new booking is confirmed, so you pay less for exactly the same stay.

> Chart: Geographic arbitrage (other countries, at checkout) and time arbitrage (later moments, after you pay).

This only works on a refundable rate, so when two prices are close, the flexible one is often the better choice. It keeps the door open for a lower price later. More detail is in [what to do when a hotel price drops after booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hotel-price-drop-after-booking.html).

## How to judge any AI travel assistant or browser extension

Whether you try a travel extension, a chatbot or a personal AI agent like Arbitrica, these questions separate a useful agent from a gimmick:

- **Does it show the final total?** A price before taxes and fees is not a price. Look for tools that work with the amount you will actually be charged.

- **Does it confirm the hotel is identical?** Same property, same dates, same number of guests. A similar hotel down the street is not a saving.

- **Can you review before paying?** You should always see what is being booked and approve the payment yourself.

- **What are the cancellation terms?** Read them on the final review screen. A lower price with stricter terms may or may not be worth it to you.

- **What permissions does it ask for?** Browser extensions request access to pages. Check what the extension needs and why.

TipAsk any AI assistant the same two questions before you trust its price: is this the identical hotel on the same terms, and is this the total I will be charged? If it cannot answer both, compare the totals yourself.

## Beyond hotels: AI that saves money on travel and more

If you are looking for AI that saves money on travel, hotels are the obvious start because the amounts are large. The mechanisms are not limited to hotels, though. The same geographic and time arbitrage applies to flights, car rentals, event tickets and online shopping. Arbitrica's agent uses the same approach for [Amazon purchases](https://arbitrica.com/blog/amazon-prices-different-countries.html) and for [event tickets](https://arbitrica.com/blog/event-ticket-price-drops.html): search the same item from 195 countries at checkout, validate it is identical with all taxes and fees, and prepare the purchase so you only review and pay.

AI can already pick a good hotel for you. The question to ask is whether it also finds the lowest price for that hotel, and whether it can prove the price is real before you pay.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can AI book a hotel for me?

AI agents can find hotels, check details and prepare a booking. Well-designed agents leave the final review and payment to you. Arbitrica prepares the booking at the lowest price it finds, and you review and pay.

### Is autonomous hotel booking AI safe to use?

It is as safe as the agent's design. Look for tools that show the full total with taxes and fees, confirm the hotel is identical, and never pay without your approval.

### Does an AI travel assistant browser extension find better prices than booking sites?

Most assistants search from your own country, so they find the same prices you would. Arbitrica, a personal AI agent that lives in your browser, searches the same hotel from 195 countries, where different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions can mean a lower total.

### How much can AI hotel booking save?

It depends on the hotel and dates. The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper from another country. In one real case Arbitrica earned a user $347.12 on a $1,527.39 stay.

### Does Arbitrica only work for hotels?

No. Agent Butler is the in-chat agent for hotels, and the same mechanisms apply to Amazon purchases, event tickets, flights and other purchases.

# AI hotel price tracker

What the category does, the three problems it solves, and eight trackers compared on countries searched, timing and whether they prepare the rebooking.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/ai-hotel-price-tracker.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: AI agents

## Key takeaways

- An AI hotel price tracker watches hotel prices automatically and finds a lower price for the same hotel, at checkout or after you book.
- The most useful trackers search from more than one country, keep searching until free cancellation ends, and prepare the rebooking.
- A lower price only counts if it is for the identical hotel and includes all taxes and fees.
- Most trackers search from one country; Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout.
- Pruvo, once the best-known post-booking tracker, moved to business-only in 2026.

An AI hotel price tracker is software that watches hotel prices for you and finds a lower price than the one you are about to pay or have already paid. The most useful ones search from more than one country, keep searching after you book, and prepare the rebooking for you. Arbitrica is built around all three; this page explains the category and what to look for.

## What is an AI hotel price tracker?

**Short answer:** An AI hotel price tracker is software that watches hotel prices automatically and finds a lower price for the same hotel, either at checkout or after you have booked. The better ones search from several countries, keep searching until free cancellation ends, and prepare the rebooking so you do not have to.

These trackers use automation and price-history data to find hotel prices lower than what you have paid or are about to pay. The "AI" part is real for some products (those that use models to predict price drops, classify rate types and decide when to rebook) and marketing for others (a simple scheduled scraper does not need a large model to work).

The category has grown because hotel pricing has become harder to read. The same hotel can be sold at many different prices on the same night, by different sellers, in different countries, in different currencies and with different cancellation policies. No person can check all of them. Software can.

## What problems does an AI hotel price tracker solve?

**Short answer:** Three problems: finding the lowest price for the hotel at the moment of booking, including from other countries; finding a lower price after you have paid, while you can still cancel; and acting on that lower price, which most people forget to do by hand. The best trackers handle all three; most handle one.

### Problem 1: finding the lowest price at checkout

When you are about to book, the price you see on the booking site or the chain's own site is not necessarily the lowest price for that hotel. Different countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions, so searching the same hotel from another country can open up prices you cannot get from your own country. A good tracker runs that search while you are at checkout and shows you the lowest result.

> Chart: In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler’s own country. The typical gap was 20–40%.

The gaps are large enough to matter. In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, and the typical gap was 20-40%.

### Problem 2: finding a lower price after you book

After you have paid, hotel prices keep moving with demand, cancellations and inventory. If your reservation has free cancellation, you can cancel and rebook at a lower price until the window closes. A tracker keeps searching during that window so you do not have to. The guide to [hotel price drops after booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hotel-price-drop-after-booking.html) explains why this happens.

### Problem 3: acting on the lower price

Acting on a lower price is the step people skip most often. Many people get an alert, mean to rebook and never do. The most advanced trackers prepare the rebooking themselves: the lower-priced reservation is set up and confirmed first, then the original is cancelled.

## How does an AI hotel price tracker work?

**Short answer:** Trackers check hotel prices from several sellers at intervals. The more advanced ones search the same hotel from many countries, estimate when a price is likely to drop again, validate that a lower price is for the identical hotel with all taxes and fees, and prepare the rebooking. Most trackers do only the first step.

The hard parts sit behind that list. Coverage is one: searching the same hotel from many countries at once is impossible by hand and difficult to run at scale. Validation is another: a lower price that leaves out taxes, or belongs to a different hotel or rate, is not a saving. The cancellation step is the third, because each seller has its own rules. Trackers that handle these well turn alerts into real savings; the rest send alerts that rarely become money you actually earn.

> Chart: At checkout Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries, checks it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price.

## The eight AI hotel price trackers in 2026

The category includes personal AI agents, browser extensions and cloud-only services. Here are the eight main trackers, described from what each product says about itself:

| Tracker | Search at checkout | Search after booking | Countries searched | Prepares rebooking |

| Arbitrica | Yes | Core approach (until free cancellation ends) | 195 | Core approach |

| RoomHawk | No | Yes, price alerts | 1 | No |

| Pruvo | No | Business-only since 2026 | 1 | No |

| RatePunk | Yes | Price alerts | 1 | No |

| Repriced | No | Yes | Not stated | Yes, rebooks or secures a credit |

| Hopper | Yes, in its own app | No, stops at booking | 1 | No |

| Hotel Ninja | Yes, compares booking sites | No | 1 | No |

| OneAir | No | Yes | Not stated | Yes, says it rebooks automatically |

Arbitrica's search after booking is part of the time-arbitrage mechanism it developed: the search from 195 countries is repeated at many points in time until the free-cancellation window ends, and a rebooking at the lower price is prepared. The new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled. For a full review of each tracker, see our [best hotel price trackers in 2026](https://arbitrica.com/blog/best-hotel-price-trackers-2026.html) article and the list of [best hotel rebooking tools](https://arbitrica.com/best-hotel-rebooking-tools.html).

> Chart: Multiple-time arbitrage: the search repeats after a refundable booking. The new booking is confirmed first; only then is the original cancelled.

## How do I choose the right AI hotel price tracker?

**Short answer:** Ask four questions. Do you book international hotels? Pick a tracker that searches from many countries; Arbitrica searches from 195. Will you act on alerts? If not, pick one that prepares the rebooking. Does it check the full price? Make sure taxes and fees are included. Do you buy more than hotels? Most trackers cover one category.

**Do you book international hotels?** If yes, you want a tracker that searches from more than one country. The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when searched from another country, and single-country trackers miss that entirely. Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries.

**Will you act on alerts?** If you have ever ignored a price-drop email, you want a tracker that prepares the rebooking for you. Repriced and OneAir say they rebook automatically. Arbitrica's approach prepares a rebooking at the lower price, combined with the search from 195 countries.

**Does it check the full price?** A lower headline price is not a saving if taxes and fees push it back up, or if it belongs to a different hotel or rate. Arbitrica validates that the lower price is for the identical hotel, includes all taxes and fees, and will not suddenly change.

**Do you buy more than hotels?** Most trackers in the table are hotel-only. Arbitrica's mechanisms also apply to online shopping such as Amazon, flights, car rentals, event tickets and subscriptions.

**Are you booking for a company?** Most trackers are built for one traveler and one reservation. Arbitrica serves companies too: teams traveling to trade shows and conferences, operations managers and travel managers, with the same search from 195 countries on every booking.

## Questions to ask before you trust a tracker

- **What happens if the rebooking fails?** The original reservation should stay in place unless a new booking is confirmed.

- **Which rate types does it watch?** A tracker that confuses a non-refundable rate with a flexible one will send you alerts that are not real savings.

- **Does it know your cancellation deadline?** The search is only useful until free cancellation ends.

- **How does it make money?** Some trackers earn affiliate commission on the new booking, which is fine but worth knowing.

## Does Arbitrica really search 195 countries?

Yes. When you reach checkout, Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries in real time and finds the lowest price on Earth for it at a different seller from the one you are on. It validates that the lower price is for the identical hotel, includes all taxes and fees, and will not suddenly change. Then it prepares the booking so you only review and pay. One Arbitrica user was offered a hotel on Booking for $1,527.39. Arbitrica found the same hotel for $1,180.27 and earned the user $347.12, or 23%.

## What about VPN-based alternatives?

Travelers have long tried this by hand with a VPN: connect to another country, search again, note the price, repeat. It can work for a country or two, but each search takes time, and doing it for 195 countries is impossible in practice. You would also need to check every result for taxes, fees and rate conditions yourself. Arbitrica does the full search and the checks for you.

See our [full explainer on why the same hotel can cost less when searched from another country](https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-different-prices-vpn-explained.html) for more detail, or the direct comparison of a [VPN and Arbitrica](https://arbitrica.com/blog/vpn-vs-arbitrica-hotel-booking.html).

## Frequently asked questions

### How much money does an AI hotel price tracker actually save?

It depends on the tracker, how often you travel and where you book. Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year. In one real case, a user was offered a hotel on Booking for $1,527.39; Arbitrica found the same hotel for $1,180.27 and earned the user $347.12 (23%). The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when searched from another country.

### Will the hotel know I rebooked at a lower rate?

The hotel sees one cancelled reservation and one new reservation, the same thing it would see if you rebooked by hand. Cancelling within a free-cancellation window carries no penalty under the terms of that booking.

### Is this legal?

Searching for the same hotel from other countries is shopping around, and cancelling a refundable reservation within its free-cancellation window is part of the booking terms you agreed to. Read the terms of each booking, since some rates come with their own conditions.

### Do AI hotel price trackers work for award redemptions?

Most do not. Award redemptions (using points or miles) follow different inventory and pricing rules. For award travel, tools like Seats.aero and Roame are purpose-built. Arbitrica works on cash prices.

### What is the difference between an AI hotel price tracker and a metasearch engine like Kayak or Trivago?

Metasearch engines show prices from several sellers at one moment, searched from your own country. They do not keep searching after you book, do not search from other countries and do not prepare a rebooking. An AI hotel price tracker is built for the savings that start at checkout and continue after you book.

# The AI agent that finds the lowest price: how a personal shopping agent works

Sellers have revenue managers and pricing engines. Here is what a buy-side AI agent does for you, and what to expect from one.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/ai-shopping-agent-lowest-price.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: AI agents

## Key takeaways

- A personal AI agent for prices searches for the identical item in many markets and prepares the purchase at the lowest validated total.
- Sellers use revenue management and dynamic pricing to move prices up; a buy-side agent works for the consumer instead.
- An agent must match the identical item and compare the full price with all taxes and fees, or a lower number can cost more.
- The human should approve the payment: the agent prepares everything, and you review and pay.
- In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country.

An entire industry works to move the prices you pay upward. Revenue managers, yield teams, dynamic pricing engines and personalization systems decide, every hour, how much the same hotel, product or ticket should cost you. Consumers have had almost nothing on their side of that table. A personal AI agent that finds the lowest price is the missing half: software that works for the buyer, searches every market for the identical item and gets it at the global minimum before you pay.

## What a personal AI agent for prices actually does

Most shopping software stops at information. A price alert tells you a number changed. A comparison site lists offers and leaves the rest to you. An AI shopping agent goes further: it takes a goal ("buy this exact item at the lowest real price") and carries out the steps needed to reach it.

For prices, those steps are fairly specific:

- Notice that you are about to buy something, at the moment the decision is being made.

- Identify exactly what the item is: the model, the hotel and dates, the seat section, the terms.

- Search for that identical item in as many markets as possible.

- Throw out offers that are not truly the same item or that hide extra costs.

- Prepare the purchase at the lowest validated price, so the person only has to review and pay.

The phrase "autonomous AI booking" often gets used loosely for this. In practice the useful version is autonomous in the search and the preparation, and human in the final decision. That split matters, and we come back to it below.

## Sell side and buy side: why consumers need their own agent

Financial markets have a sell side and a buy side, and each has its own professionals. Consumer prices have a very well-staffed sell side. Hotels run revenue management systems that reprice stays as demand changes. Online stores test prices, run promotions in some countries and not others, and use different sellers and channels for the same product. Ticketing platforms use demand-based pricing for popular events. All of this is legal, normal business, and all of it is designed to capture as much as possible of what each buyer is willing to pay.

> Chart: Different countries get different inventory, channels, local rates, promotions and currencies, and pricing algorithms move rates all day.

The buy side, for an individual consumer, has traditionally been a browser and some patience. You can open a few tabs, try a coupon code and hope. You cannot search the same item from dozens of countries, check every seller, validate that each offer is identical and redo the search every day until your cancellation window closes. A personal AI agent for price optimization is the consumer's version of a buy-side desk: it does that work at machine speed and reports back only what is worth acting on.

In April 2025, Visa and Mastercard both announced programs designed to let AI agents make purchases on a user's behalf, Visa Intelligent Commerce and Mastercard Agent Pay. Payment networks building rails for agents is a strong sign that buying through an agent is becoming a normal way to shop.

## Why the agent must validate the identical item and the full price

Finding a lower number is easy. Finding a lower number for the same thing is the hard part, and it is where a careless agent would cost you money instead of earning it.

### Identical item

Two offers can look the same and differ in ways that matter. A hotel listing may be a different room category, include or exclude breakfast, or carry a non-refundable rate where you expected free cancellation. A product may be a regional variant with a different model number, power plug, language setting or warranty. An event ticket may be in a different section or come from a resale listing with different transfer rules. An agent that finds the lowest price has to match on the details that define the item, not on the title.

### Full price

The headline number is rarely the price you pay. Hotels add city taxes and resort fees late in the booking flow. Online orders add shipping, import duties and payment charges. Ticket platforms add service and delivery fees at the last step. The only fair comparison is the total at checkout, in your currency, with every tax and fee included. A good agent compares totals and also checks that the price will hold, so you are not shown a number that changes on the final screen.

TipWhether you use an agent or search by hand, write down the full checkout total for your first offer, including every fee. Judge every alternative against that one number.

## Why the human approves the payment

An agent can do the searching, matching, validating and preparing. Spending your money should still be your call. There are good reasons for that line:

- **Preferences the agent cannot see.** You might prefer a certain cancellation policy, a delivery date or a seller you have used before.

- **Accountability.** Payments are hard to reverse. A final human review catches the rare case where something looks wrong.

- **Trust.** People are more comfortable using an agent when they know nothing is charged without their approval.

So the sensible model is an agent that prepares everything at the lowest price and stops at the payment step. You see what was found, the full price and the terms, and you decide.

## Geographic arbitrage: the same item from another country

The biggest source of savings is where an item is bought from. Different countries get access to different inventory, sales channels, local rates and promotions. Searching the same item from another country can open up lower prices you cannot get from your own country. This is geographic price arbitrage, and the guide to [what geographic price arbitrage is](https://arbitrica.com/blog/what-is-geographic-price-arbitrage.html) explains it in more depth.

Hotels show it most clearly. In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, and the typical gap was 20-40%. A 2024 NordVPN study found that travel bookings made through US websites came out up to 70% higher than through websites elsewhere (its largest gap was a car rental); a seven-night stay in a triple room at a Milan hotel for a family of three cost about $1,216 searched from the US and $1,012 searched from Italy.

> Chart: In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler’s own country. The typical gap was 20–40%.

The same logic applies to [buying online from another country](https://arbitrica.com/blog/buy-online-cheaper-from-another-country.html), where an identical product can be listed by different sellers and stores at different prices, and to event tickets sold through several channels. Across categories, the same item is often 5-30% cheaper elsewhere. Doing this by hand means a VPN, one country at a time, and a lot of guesswork about which countries to try. Nobody can check 195 countries manually before every purchase.

## Time arbitrage: the same item at a later moment

The second source of savings is when an item is bought. Prices keep moving after you pay. If your purchase can still be cancelled or returned, a later drop is money you can still earn.

- **Hotels.** Book a refundable rate, keep checking until free cancellation ends, and rebook if the identical hotel gets cheaper.

- **Online shopping.** Pre-orders and items with a return window can be bought again at a lower price and the first order returned or cancelled.

- **Event tickets.** Prices for many events move as the date approaches, and some purchases can be changed. See [how event ticket prices drop](https://arbitrica.com/blog/event-ticket-price-drops.html).

Our article on [time arbitrage](https://arbitrica.com/blog/time-arbitrage-explained.html) covers the details. The key safety rule is order: the new purchase must be confirmed before the original is cancelled, so you are never left without a booking.

## How Arbitrica works as a personal AI agent

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent built for the buy side. It meets you at checkout, when you are about to pay, and searches the same item from 195 countries. It validates that the offer is identical, with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price on Earth. You review and pay.

> Chart: At checkout Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries, checks it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price.

Arbitrica always looks for the lower price at a different provider or seller than the one you are on, so the result is a real alternative rather than the same offer again. The provider is never the point; the identical item at the lowest total is.

For time arbitrage, Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after you buy, while free cancellation or a return window is still open. When the identical item becomes available at a lower price, a new purchase is prepared and confirmed first, and only then is the original cancelled.

A real example: a hotel offered at $1,527.39 on Booking.com was found by Arbitrica for $1,180.27 for the identical hotel, earning the user $347.12 (23%). Research demonstrated average earnings of $47 per hotel booking, $34 per online purchase and $107 per event ticket purchase. Companies use the same approach: travel managers and operations managers booking teams into trade shows and conferences face the same pricing systems at a larger scale. The full flow is described on [how it works](https://arbitrica.com/how-it-works.html).

## What to look for in an AI agent that finds the lowest price

- **It searches widely**An agent that only checks a few stores or your own country misses most of the spread. Coverage of many countries is where the large gaps are.

- **It matches the identical item**Model numbers, room types, dates, seat sections and terms must match, not just the product name.

- **It compares full totals**Taxes, fees, shipping and duties included, in your currency.

- **It keeps working after you pay**Repeating the search inside a cancellation or return window adds a second chance to earn.

- **It leaves the payment to you**Preparation can be automatic; spending your money should not be.

Even without any agent, these are the habits that save money: check the full price, look beyond your own country, prefer flexible terms and keep checking until you can no longer change the purchase. An agent simply does all of it, every time, for every purchase.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a personal AI shopping agent?

It is software that works for the buyer: it notices a purchase, searches for the identical item in other markets, validates the full price and prepares the purchase at the lowest price for you to approve.

### Does an AI shopping agent pay for me?

The safest model leaves payment to you. The agent searches, validates and prepares everything, then you review the item, terms and total before you pay.

### Why would the same item be cheaper from another country?

Different countries get access to different inventory, sales channels, local rates and promotions, so searching the same item from another country can open up lower prices.

### Does this only work for hotels?

No. Geographic and time arbitrage also apply to online shopping and event tickets, as well as flights, car rentals and other purchases with prices that differ by market or move over time.

# Hopper alternative

Hopper forecasts prices and sells price freezes from one market. Here is how a search from 195 countries at checkout, plus a repeated search after you book, compares.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/alternative-to-hopper.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Comparisons

## Key takeaways

- Hopper is a booking app built around price prediction, Price Freeze and Carrot Cash rewards.
- Hopper states that it does not price-match hotel reservations, and it stops watching once you book.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout and validates the identical hotel with all taxes and fees included.
- Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after you book until free cancellation ends, and the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.
- Hopper fits domestic flights booked on a phone; Arbitrica fits international hotels and refundable bookings.

Hopper is a booking app built around price prediction and price freezes. It stops watching once you book, and it searches from one country. Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser and shows up at checkout, searches the same hotel from 195 countries, checks that the lower price is for the identical hotel with all taxes and fees included, and prepares the booking so you only review and pay. Its approach then repeats the search after you book, until the free-cancellation window ends.

## Why people search for a Hopper alternative

**Short answer:** Hopper made its name on flight-price prediction and grew into one of the largest travel-booking apps in North America. Two limits push people to look elsewhere: Hopper does not keep watching a reservation after it is booked, and it does not look at what the same hotel costs when searched from other countries.

Hopper's product is flight and hotel booking with predictive pricing. It tells you whether to book now or wait, sells Price Freeze, which holds a price for a fee (up to 60 days on hotels, with the protection capped; Hopper's launch announcement said it would cover up to $100 of an increase), and runs the Carrot Cash rewards program. Hopper also states that it does not price-match hotel reservations. If the rate for your hotel falls after you book, Hopper does not act on it.

## What does Arbitrica do that Hopper does not?

**Short answer:** It works on two kinds of arbitrage that Hopper does not touch.

- **Geographic arbitrage, live at checkout**Different countries get access to different inventory, sales channels, local rates and promotions. Searching the same hotel from another country can open up prices you cannot get from your own country. Doing that by hand with a VPN, one country at a time, works for three or four countries at most. Arbitrica searches from all 195.

- **Multiple-time arbitrage, after you book**Hotel rates keep moving after you pay. Arbitrica's approach repeats the search at many points in time until your free-cancellation window ends, and when it finds a lower price for the identical hotel it prepares the new booking. The new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.

> Chart: Geographic arbitrage (other countries, at checkout) and time arbitrage (later moments, after you pay).

In both cases the provider is not the point. The lower price comes from a different seller from the one you are on: Booking, Expedia, the hotel chain or anyone else. Arbitrica validates that it is the same hotel, the same dates and the same conditions, that taxes and fees are included, and that the price will not suddenly change at payment.

One real example: a hotel offered at $1,527.39 on Booking was found for $1,180.27. Arbitrica earned that traveler $347.12, or 23%, on a single stay.

> Chart: A real booking: offered at $1,527.39, found for $1,180.27 for the identical hotel. Arbitrica earned the user $347.12 (23%).

## Side-by-side: Hopper vs Arbitrica

| What it does | Hopper | Arbitrica |

| Searches before you pay | Yes, from one country | Yes, from 195 countries |

| Geographic arbitrage | No | Yes |

| Keeps searching after you book | No, stops at booking | Yes, until the cancellation window ends |

| Prepares the rebooking | No | Yes |

| Finds the lower price from any seller | Within its own booking flow | Yes, whoever sells it |

| Checks identical hotel, taxes and fees | Not applicable | Yes |

| Price prediction | Yes | Not the focus |

| Price Freeze | Yes, for a fee | No |

| Beyond hotels and flights | Car rentals in the app | Same mechanisms for car rentals, event tickets, online shopping and subscriptions |

| Type | Booking app, mainly on iOS and Android | Personal AI agent (lives in your browser) |

## Prediction versus searching from 195 countries

A price prediction answers one question: is the price you see in your own market likely to go up or down? That is useful for flights, where one market and one fare matter. For hotels it leaves out the bigger gap. In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, and the typical gap was 20-40%. A forecast built on one market cannot find that difference, however accurate it is.

The two approaches also treat timing differently. Price Freeze lets you pay to hold a price before you commit. A refundable booking does something similar without a separate fee: you hold the hotel, and if the price falls before the cancellation deadline you can book again at the lower price. That is the window Arbitrica's approach keeps working in. The guide to [what to do when a hotel price drops after booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hotel-price-drop-after-booking.html) covers the manual version.

## When is Hopper the better choice?

**Short answer:** Hopper is the better pick if you mostly book domestic flights on your phone and want guidance on when to buy, or if you collect Carrot Cash. Price Freeze is also useful for a trip you are fairly sure about but cannot commit to yet.

## When is Arbitrica the better choice?

**Short answer:** Arbitrica is the better pick for international hotels, and for anyone who books refundable. The same hotel is often 5 to 30% cheaper when searched from another country, and a forecast cannot find that gap because it only looks at one market. The repeated search after booking adds a second chance to pay less on the same reservation. Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

> Chart: The same item, with the same dates and terms, is often 5–30% cheaper bought from another country or at another moment.

The same mechanisms are not limited to hotels. Flights, car rentals, event tickets, pre-orders and delayed-shipment purchases on sites like Amazon, and subscriptions all vary by country or come with a cancellation or return window, so the same search from 195 countries and the same repeated search over time apply to them too.

## What other Hopper alternatives exist?

**Short answer:** The category is fragmented, and most tools cover one piece.

- **Google Hotels and Google Flights** track prices and email you when they move. They do not rebook anything.

- **RatePunk** checks the same hotel on several booking sites before you book, with price alerts. It does not search from other countries.

- **RoomHawk** focuses on price alerts for a hotel after you book.

- **Pruvo** was the best-known post-booking hotel tracker until 2026, when it moved to business-only and stopped serving travelers. Arbitrica works for both: individual travelers, and companies whose teams travel to trade shows and conferences, along with their operations managers and travel managers.

We are not aware of another product that combines a search from 195 countries at checkout with a repeated search after booking and a prepared rebooking. For the wider picture, see our [2026 review of the main hotel price trackers](https://arbitrica.com/blog/best-hotel-price-trackers-2026.html) and our list of the [best hotel rebooking tools](https://arbitrica.com/best-hotel-rebooking-tools.html).

## How do I switch from Hopper to Arbitrica?

**Short answer:** There is nothing to migrate. Hopper is an app with its own booking flow; Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser and appears at checkout when you book on the web. Keep Hopper on your phone for flight predictions if you like them. The two do not conflict.

## Frequently asked questions

### Will I lose my Hopper Carrot Cash if I use Arbitrica?

No. Arbitrica does not interact with your Hopper account. Any Carrot Cash you have collected stays available for redemption inside Hopper.

### Does Arbitrica predict hotel prices like Hopper does?

No. Hopper estimates whether a price will rise or fall. Arbitrica looks for the lowest price that exists right now by searching the same hotel from 195 countries, and its approach repeats that search after you book until the free-cancellation window ends. On hotels, the gap between countries is often larger than anything a forecast can win you.

### Can I use Arbitrica on the Hopper app itself?

No. Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser and works on web checkouts such as Booking.com, Expedia, Hotels.com, Agoda and hotel chain sites. Bookings made inside the Hopper mobile app are not visible to it.

### Does Arbitrica only work for hotels?

No. Hotels are where the gap between countries is easiest to see, but the same mechanisms apply to flights, car rentals, event tickets, online shopping such as Amazon, and subscriptions: anything sold at different prices in different countries or with a cancellation or return window.

# Amazon prices in different countries: why the same product costs more or less

Different stores, sellers, taxes and promotions mean one product has many prices. Here is what to check before you buy from another country.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/amazon-prices-different-countries.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Online shopping

## Key takeaways

- Each Amazon country store has its own sellers, stock, promotions, taxes and currency, so the same product can carry different prices.
- Before buying from another country, match the exact model number and check the seller, warranty, shipping, import duties and returns.
- Compare the delivered total in your currency with every tax, duty and fee included, never the listed price.
- The United States suspended duty-free de minimis treatment for low-value imports from all countries from August 29, 2025.
- Arbitrica searches the same product from 195 countries at checkout, validates it is identical and prepares the purchase at the lowest price.

Look up the same product on Amazon in two different countries and you will often see two different prices. Sometimes the gap is small and disappears once shipping is added. Sometimes the same model, from the same manufacturer, costs noticeably less in another country or from another seller. Knowing why that happens, and what to check before you buy, is the difference between earning a real saving and paying for a surprise at customs.

## Why Amazon prices differ between countries

Amazon runs separate stores for many countries, such as amazon.com in the US, amazon.co.uk in the UK, amazon.de in Germany and amazon.co.jp in Japan. Each store has its own catalog, its own mix of sellers, its own stock and its own promotions. The same product can sit in all of them at different prices for several reasons:

- **Different sellers.** On any Amazon store, a product page can be served by Amazon itself or by third-party sellers. Who holds stock in each country, and how much they want to clear it, varies.

- **Local pricing and promotions.** Manufacturers and retailers set prices per market, and sales events, coupons and clearance happen at different times in different countries.

- **Taxes in the displayed price.** In the UK and the EU, prices shown to consumers include VAT. In the US, sales tax is usually added at checkout. A price that looks higher may simply include tax that another store adds later.

- **Currency.** Exchange rates move, while listed prices often stay put for a while, so one market can drift cheaper or more expensive relative to another.

- **Local competition.** A product that is heavily discounted by competing retailers in one country tends to be cheaper on Amazon there too.

> Chart: Different countries get different inventory, channels, local rates, promotions and currencies, and pricing algorithms move rates all day.

None of this is unusual. It is how prices work when the same product is sold through many channels in many markets. The result is that "the price" of a product is really a range, and where you buy from decides where in that range you land.

## Same product, different price, different seller

Price differences are not only between countries. Within a single store, the same listing can have several offers: new from Amazon, new from a third-party seller, renewed, or used. Other retailers may sell the identical model too. When people search for "same product different price different country", the cheapest option often turns out to be a different seller in another market rather than the store they started on.

That is useful, but it is also where mistakes happen. A lower price from an unfamiliar seller is only a good deal if the item is identical and the seller is reliable.

## What to check before you buy from another country

Before you buy, go through each of these. Skipping one is how a saving on the listed price turns into a loss.

### Identical model number

Manufacturers often sell regional variants. A laptop may have a different keyboard layout, a camera may have a different kit lens, a phone may support different network bands, and an appliance may have a different plug or voltage. Match the exact model number or part number, not just the product name and photo.

### The seller

Check who sells and ships the item, the seller's ratings and how long it has been selling. "Sold by" and "Ships from" can be different businesses, and that affects returns and support.

### Warranty

Some manufacturer warranties are international; others only apply in the country or region of purchase. Check the manufacturer's warranty terms for the exact model before buying abroad, especially for electronics and appliances.

### Shipping and delivery time

International shipping can be expensive and slow, and not every product ships to every country. Check whether the seller ships to your address and add the shipping cost to the total.

### Import duties and taxes

Buying across borders can trigger import duties, VAT or sales tax, and carrier handling fees. On some international orders Amazon collects an estimated amount at checkout to cover these. Rules change, too: the United States suspended its duty-free de minimis treatment for low-value imports from all countries from August 29, 2025. Check current rules for your country before you order.

### Returns

A return to another country can cost more than the saving. Check the return window, who pays return shipping and whether the seller accepts international returns.

TipCompare one number only: the final total delivered to your door, in your currency, with shipping, duties, taxes and fees included. A listed price is not a delivered price.

## A quick checklist

| Check | What to look for | Why it matters |

| Model number | Exact match, including region code | Regional variants can differ in plugs, bands, languages or accessories. |

| Seller | Who sells and who ships, ratings, history | Affects authenticity, support and returns. |

| Warranty | International or country-specific | A country-only warranty may not help you at home. |

| Shipping | Ships to you, cost, delivery time | Shipping can erase the gap on low-priced items. |

| Duties and taxes | Collected at checkout or on delivery | Can add a large share to the total. |

| Returns | Window, cost, international returns | An expensive return can wipe out the saving. |

## When buying from another country makes sense

Cross-border buying tends to work best for items that are easy to verify and easy to ship: branded electronics with a clear model number and an international warranty, books, toys, cosmetics, tools and accessories. It works less well for very heavy or bulky items, for products with strict regional differences, and for anything you may need to return. The guide to [buying online cheaper from another country](https://arbitrica.com/blog/buy-online-cheaper-from-another-country.html) walks through more categories and examples of what to look for.

The same product is often 5-30% cheaper elsewhere, but the real question is always the delivered total. A modest gap on an expensive item is usually worth more than a big percentage on a low-priced one.

> Chart: The same item, with the same dates and terms, is often 5–30% cheaper bought from another country or at another moment.

## Why checking by hand rarely finds the best price

Checking two or three Amazon stores is manageable. Checking every country store, every seller and every other retailer that stocks the identical model is not. Each one means a new site, a new currency, a new set of shipping and tax rules, and a new seller to vet. Some offers are only shown when you search from that country, which means a VPN and one country at a time. Most people stop after a couple of tries, which is why the lowest price usually goes unfound. This is geographic price arbitrage, explained in more detail in [what is geographic price arbitrage](https://arbitrica.com/blog/what-is-geographic-price-arbitrage.html).

## How Arbitrica finds the same product at a lower price

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that meets you at checkout. When you are about to buy, it searches the same product from 195 countries, at other sellers and stores than the one you are on. It validates that the item is identical, matching the model and the offer rather than the title, and checks the full price with taxes and fees included. Then it prepares the purchase at the lowest price on Earth, and you review and pay.

> Chart: At checkout Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries, checks it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price.

Research showed that people earn on average $34 per online purchase this way, and up to $3,000 a year. For orders with a return window or a delayed shipment, Arbitrica's approach also repeats the search after you buy; if the identical product becomes available at a lower price, a new purchase is prepared and confirmed before the original is cancelled. The idea is covered in [time arbitrage explained](https://arbitrica.com/blog/time-arbitrage-explained.html), and the bigger picture of buy-side agents in [the AI agent that finds the lowest price](https://arbitrica.com/blog/ai-shopping-agent-lowest-price.html).

Companies buying equipment or supplies for teams face the same price differences at a larger scale, and operations managers use the same approach for recurring purchases.

## Bottom line

Amazon prices differ between countries because each store has its own sellers, stock, promotions, taxes and currency. That creates real opportunities, as long as you match the exact model, vet the seller, check the warranty and returns, and compare the delivered total with every duty and fee included. Do that, by hand or with an agent searching for you, and buying from another country becomes a reliable way to pay less for the identical product.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why are Amazon prices different in different countries?

Each Amazon store has its own sellers, stock, local promotions, tax rules and currency. The same product can therefore be listed at different prices in different countries.

### Is it cheaper to buy from Amazon in another country?

Sometimes. It depends on the delivered total after shipping, import duties, taxes and fees, and on whether the model, warranty and return terms suit you.

### Do I pay import duties when buying from Amazon abroad?

You may. On some international orders Amazon collects an estimated amount at checkout; otherwise duties and taxes can be charged on delivery. Check the current rules for your country.

### How do I make sure it is the same product?

Match the exact model or part number, including any region code, and check accessories, plugs, language and warranty, rather than relying on the product name or photo.

# Arbitrica vs. Pruvo: which saves you more?

Pruvo tracked one booking on one platform from one country, and it now serves businesses only. Here is how the two approaches differ.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/arbitrica-vs-pruvo.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Comparisons

## Key takeaways

- Pruvo tracked a booking you forwarded by email for price drops on the same platform, from one country.
- Web Travel Group announced its acquisition of Pruvo, which now presents itself as a business-to-business platform and no longer supports consumer bookings.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout, then repeats the search after booking until free cancellation ends.
- With Arbitrica, the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled, and you review and pay.
- Arbitrica serves both consumers and companies, including trade-show teams, operations managers and travel managers.

Pruvo was one of the best-known hotel price trackers for travelers who wanted to catch price drops after booking. Arbitrica works on the same problem from a different direction. This comparison looks at how each one finds a lower price, where the saving comes from, and how much of the work is left to you.

Pruvo has since moved away from consumer bookings and now presents itself as a business-to-business platform (see the update at the end of this article). So this comparison covers both sides: travelers who used Pruvo, or a tracker built on the same model, and companies weighing Pruvo's business offering. Arbitrica serves both consumers and companies.

## How Pruvo works

Pruvo monitored hotel prices after you booked. You forwarded your booking confirmation email to check@pruvo.com, and Pruvo began tracking the rate. If the price dropped on the same platform, Pruvo sent you an alert. You then cancelled your old reservation and rebooked at the lower rate yourself.

Pruvo offered basic tracking at no charge, and a premium tier added priority monitoring and multi-booking management. The system was straightforward and did what it promised. Today Pruvo describes itself as an AI platform for travel companies, built around rebooking hotel reservations when prices fall.

## How Arbitrica works

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser. It meets you at the checkout when you are about to pay for a hotel, searches the same hotel from 195 countries, and finds the lowest price on Earth for it, at a different seller from the one you are on. It then prepares the booking, so you only review and pay.

The approach rests on two families of mechanisms:

- **Geographic arbitrage.** Different countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions. Searching the same hotel from another country can open up lower prices you cannot get from your own country.

- **Time arbitrage.** Live arbitrage runs the search at checkout, in real time. Multiple-time arbitrage repeats the search after you book, until the free-cancellation window ends, and prepares a re-booking at the lower price. The new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.

> Chart: Geographic arbitrage (other countries, at checkout) and time arbitrage (later moments, after you pay).

Before a lower price counts, Arbitrica validates that it is for the identical hotel, that it includes all taxes and fees, and that it will not suddenly change at the payment step.

## The core difference: where the saving comes from

Pruvo checked for price drops in the same country and on the same platform where you originally booked. If you booked from the US on Booking.com, Pruvo monitored the US Booking.com price. That catches drops over time, but it never looks at the prices available from other countries.

Arbitrica starts from the other side. It searches the same hotel from 195 countries before you pay, so the price you book is already the lowest it could find. The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when searched from another country. In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country. Doing that by hand, with a VPN and one country at a time, is impossible in practice. Arbitrica's multiple-time approach then covers the drops over time that Pruvo was built for, searched from 195 countries instead of one.

## Pruvo vs. Arbitrica: feature table

| Feature | Pruvo | Arbitrica |

| How it starts | You forward a confirmation email | Meets you at the checkout when you are about to pay |

| Search before you pay (live arbitrage) | No | Yes |

| Countries searched | 1 | 195 |

| Search repeated after booking | Yes, same platform and country | Multiple-time arbitrage from 195 countries until the free-cancellation window ends |

| Identical hotel, taxes and fees validated | Tracks the booking you forwarded | Yes, before the lower price counts |

| Rebooking | Manual | Prepared for you; you review and pay |

| Type | Email-based price tracker | Personal AI agent (lives in your browser) |

| Who it serves | Now business-to-business; consumer bookings no longer supported | Consumers and companies: trade-show and conference teams, operations managers, travel managers |

| Beyond hotels | No | Same mechanisms for flights, event tickets, online shopping and more |

| Where the saving comes from | Price drops over time, one country | The same hotel from 195 countries, at checkout and over time |

## Setup and user experience

Pruvo required you to forward each booking confirmation email. If you forgot to forward a booking, Pruvo did not track it. When it found a lower rate, you got an email, and then had to go back to the booking platform, cancel the old reservation and rebook at the new rate yourself.

Arbitrica works at the moment of payment. Because it is there at the checkout, there is nothing to forward. When it finds a lower price for the identical hotel, it prepares everything, so your part is to review and pay. The multiple-time approach works the same way: the re-booking at the lower price is prepared for you, and the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled, instead of landing in your inbox as a to-do.

> Chart: Multiple-time arbitrage: the search repeats after a refundable booking. The new booking is confirmed first; only then is the original cancelled.

### Rebooking by hand safely, whichever route you take

If you still track prices yourself, a few habits stop a price drop from turning into a problem:

- **Book a refundable rate**A drop after booking is only useful if you can cancel the original without a penalty.

- **Compare totals, not nightly rates**Taxes, resort fees and payment fees can wipe out a small headline drop.

- **Match the terms exactly**Same hotel, dates, guests, meal plan and cancellation policy.

- **Book the new one first**Cancel the original only after the new confirmation arrives, so you are never left without a hotel.

## Beyond hotels

Pruvo was built for hotel bookings only. Arbitrica's mechanisms are not limited to hotels. Searching the same item from 195 countries also works for flights, car rentals, event tickets and online shopping such as Amazon orders. Repeating the search over time works for anything with a cancellation or return window, including pre-orders and subscriptions.

## For companies: Arbitrica vs. Pruvo's B2B model

With Pruvo now positioned as a business-to-business platform, the comparison matters for companies as much as for individual travelers. This article does not cover the details of Pruvo's business offering, so check its current terms directly. The model it was built on, tracking a booking for drops over time on one platform from one country, is the part that can be compared.

Arbitrica works for companies as well as consumers. Three groups get the most from it:

- **Teams traveling to trade shows and conferences.** Many people book hotels in the same city for the same dates, when hotel prices near the venue tend to rise. Each of those bookings is searched from 195 countries at the checkout, and event hotels are often booked early with free cancellation, which leaves a long window for the search to be repeated before the trip.

- **Operations managers** who book travel for staff. They get the lowest price Arbitrica finds for the identical hotel, validated with all taxes and fees, without checking countries one at a time.

- **Travel managers** responsible for hotel spend across the company. The traveler stays in the hotel they chose, on the same dates and terms, and only the price changes.

The mechanisms are the same as for a single traveler. For a company with many bookings a year, a single-country tracker leaves the larger source of price variation untouched. Read more in [business travel hotel savings for travel managers](https://arbitrica.com/blog/business-travel-hotel-savings.html) and [trade show hotel prices](https://arbitrica.com/blog/trade-show-hotel-prices.html).

## Which is better?

Pruvo was a solid choice for travelers who wanted simple post-booking alerts on one platform. It caught drops over time reliably and was easy to set up. It no longer serves consumers.

Arbitrica covers more ground, for travelers and companies alike. It searches the same hotel from 195 countries before you pay, validates that the lower price is for the identical hotel with all taxes and fees, and prepares the booking for you. Its multiple-time approach repeats that search after you book. In one real booking, Booking.com offered $1,527.39 and Arbitrica found $1,180.27 for the identical hotel, earning the user $347.12 (23%). A single-country tracker never sees a price like that. Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

> Chart: A real booking: offered at $1,527.39, found for $1,180.27 for the identical hotel. Arbitrica earned the user $347.12 (23%).

## Update: Pruvo has left the consumer market

Since this comparison was first written, Web Travel Group has announced its acquisition of Pruvo, and Pruvo now presents itself as a business-to-business platform, with consumer bookings no longer supported. Travelers who relied on it, and companies weighing their options, can look at Arbitrica, which serves both. For other replacements, see [the best hotel rebooking tools in 2026](https://arbitrica.com/best-hotel-rebooking-tools.html).

### Is Pruvo still available for travelers?

No. Pruvo now presents itself as a business-to-business platform, and consumer bookings are no longer supported.

### What is the main difference between Pruvo and Arbitrica?

Pruvo watched one booking for drops on the same platform from one country. Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout and repeats the search after booking until free cancellation ends.

### Does Arbitrica rebook automatically?

Arbitrica's approach prepares the re-booking at the lower price for you to review. The new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.

### Can companies use Arbitrica instead of Pruvo?

# Arbitrica vs. RoomHawk: full comparison

RoomHawk catches drops over time on the price you already see. Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries, before you pay and after.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/arbitrica-vs-roomhawk.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Comparisons

## Key takeaways

- RoomHawk says it tracks over 2 million hotel rooms and focuses on price drops for a stay you have chosen.
- A single-country tracker only wins when the price you already see goes down.
- The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when searched from another country, at the same moment.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout and repeats the search until free cancellation ends.
- In Arbitrica's rebooking flow the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.

RoomHawk and Arbitrica both help travelers pay less for hotels. RoomHawk focuses on watching a hotel for price drops. Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at the checkout and repeats that search over time. The two differ in scope, in automation and in the kind of saving they find.

## How RoomHawk works

RoomHawk says it searches and tracks over 2 million hotel rooms. You pick a stay, RoomHawk monitors the price, and you hear about it when the rate drops. Its focus is drops over time: rates falling because demand shifts, guests cancel or a hotel releases last-minute inventory. RoomHawk's site describes it as a way to discover hotels, compare prices and monitor price drops for a chosen stay. It also advertises AI-powered auto-rebooking, though its site does not explain how that step works.

What RoomHawk does not describe is searching the same hotel from other countries. Its tracking looks at the price available to you, and catches the moment that price goes down.

## How Arbitrica works

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser. It meets you at the checkout when you are about to pay, searches the same hotel from 195 countries, and finds the lowest price on Earth for it, at a different seller from the one you are on. It then prepares the booking, so you only review and pay.

It uses two families of mechanisms:

- **Geographic arbitrage.** Different countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions. Searching the same hotel from another country can open up lower prices you cannot get from your own country.

- **Time arbitrage.** Live arbitrage runs the search at checkout, in real time. Multiple-time arbitrage repeats the search after you book, until the free-cancellation window ends, and prepares a re-booking at the lower price. The new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.

Arbitrica validates that any lower price is for the identical hotel, includes all taxes and fees, and will not suddenly change before you pay.

## The geo-arbitrage gap: two different kinds of saving

A price tracker like RoomHawk is built for catching drops over time. A hotel that costs $250 today may drop to $220 next week because demand falls. A tracker catches that $30 saving.

Arbitrica finds a different kind of saving. Searched from Indonesia or Portugal, that same $250 hotel may come in lower right now, because those countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions. These differences exist at the same moment, and the same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper from another country.

> Chart: The same item, with the same dates and terms, is often 5–30% cheaper bought from another country or at another moment.

In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, and the typical gap was 20-40%. Searching all 195 countries by hand is impossible in practice. Arbitrica does it at the checkout, and its multiple-time approach also covers the drops over time that RoomHawk looks for.

In one real booking, Booking.com offered $1,527.39 and Arbitrica found $1,180.27 for the identical hotel, earning the user $347.12 (23%). Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

> Chart: A real booking: offered at $1,527.39, found for $1,180.27 for the identical hotel. Arbitrica earned the user $347.12 (23%).

## RoomHawk vs. Arbitrica: feature table

| Feature | RoomHawk | Arbitrica |

| Coverage | 2M+ hotel rooms (RoomHawk figure) | The hotel at your checkout, no matter who sells it |

| Geographic arbitrage | Not described | Yes, from 195 countries |

| Search before you pay (live arbitrage) | No | Yes |

| Search repeated after booking | Yes, price-drop monitoring | Multiple-time arbitrage from 195 countries until the free-cancellation window ends |

| Identical hotel, taxes and fees validated | Tracks the stay you chose | Yes, before the lower price counts |

| Rebooking | Advertises AI auto-rebooking | Prepared for you; you review and pay; new booking confirmed before the original is cancelled |

| Type | Hotel price tracker | Personal AI agent (lives in your browser) |

| Who it serves | Travelers tracking their own stays | Consumers and companies: trade-show and conference teams, operations managers, travel managers |

| Beyond hotels | No | Same mechanisms for flights, event tickets, online shopping and more |

## User experience differences

With a tracker, you set up each stay you want watched, and the system begins monitoring. Then you wait for a drop, and act on it before your cancellation deadline.

Arbitrica needs no setup per booking, because it is there at the checkout when you are about to pay. When it finds a lower price, it has already validated that the price is for the identical hotel and the same room type with all taxes and fees, and it prepares the booking so you only review and pay. In the multiple-time approach, the re-booking it prepares matches your original hotel and terms, and the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.

> Chart: Multiple-time arbitrage: the search repeats after a refundable booking. The new booking is confirmed first; only then is the original cancelled.

## An illustrative example: one trip, both kinds of saving

Say you book four nights at a city hotel for $250 a night, refundable until three days before arrival. The numbers below are made up to show the method, not real quotes.

| Moment | What a single-country tracker sees | What a search from 195 countries can see |

| At checkout | $1,000 total, the price in front of you | The same hotel at a lower total from another country, before you pay |

| Two weeks later | A drop to $920 total, if demand softens | That drop, plus any lower price available from other countries at that moment |

| After free cancellation ends | Nothing more to gain | Nothing more to gain |

The point of the example is the shape, not the numbers: a tracker only wins when the price you already see goes down. A search from other countries can win on day one and again later.

## What to check before choosing any hotel price tracker

- **When does it work?** Before you pay, after you book, or both.

- **From how many countries does it search?** One country only catches drops over time on the price you already see.

- **Does it compare totals?** Taxes and fees decide whether a drop is real.

- **Who does the rebooking?** If it is you, set a reminder for your cancellation deadline.

- **Does it confirm the new booking first?** The original should be cancelled only after the replacement is confirmed.

For a wider ranking, see [the best hotel price trackers in 2026](https://arbitrica.com/blog/best-hotel-price-trackers-2026.html).

## When RoomHawk works well

RoomHawk is a reasonable choice for travelers who want to catch drops over time on a stay they have chosen. Its large database of rooms gives broad coverage for price-drop monitoring.

## When Arbitrica is the better choice

For anyone who wants the lowest price on a hotel, in their own country or abroad, Arbitrica finds a larger kind of saving. The search from 195 countries reaches prices a single-country tracker never checks, and covering both the checkout and the time after booking means the lowest price can be found before you pay and again before the free-cancellation window closes. The same mechanisms also apply beyond hotels, to flights, event tickets and online shopping, and they serve companies as well as individual travelers: teams heading to trade shows and conferences, operations managers and travel managers. More on the after-booking side is in [hotel price drops after booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hotel-price-drop-after-booking.html) and [what geographic price arbitrage is](https://arbitrica.com/blog/what-is-geographic-price-arbitrage.html).

## Frequently asked questions

### What does RoomHawk do?

RoomHawk says it searches and tracks over 2 million hotel rooms and monitors price drops for a stay you choose. It focuses on prices falling over time.

### How is Arbitrica different from RoomHawk?

Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout, before you pay, and its multiple-time approach repeats the search after you book until free cancellation ends.

### Can I use a price tracker and Arbitrica together?

Yes. A tracker watches for drops over time, while Arbitrica finds lower prices for the identical hotel from 195 countries at checkout and over time.
