# Booking.com different prices by country and VPNs, explained

Where the price differences come from, what a VPN can and cannot do, and how to find the lowest price for the same hotel without checking countries one by one.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-different-prices-vpn-explained.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Hidden prices

## Key takeaways

- Different countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions, so the same hotel can cost less searched from another country.
- A VPN checks one country at a time, and checking all 195 countries by hand is impossible in practice.
- A 2024 NordVPN study found travel bookings made through US websites came out up to 70% higher than through websites elsewhere (its largest gap was a car rental).
- Only the final total with taxes and fees is a fair comparison between countries.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout, validates it is identical and prepares the booking for you to review and pay.

The hotel you are looking at on Booking.com can often be booked for less when the same hotel is searched from another country. Each country has access to different inventory, sales channels, local rates and promotions, so searching from somewhere else can open up prices you cannot get from your own country. A VPN lets you try one other country at a time, and checking all 195 countries by hand is impossible in practice. This guide explains where the differences come from, what a VPN can and cannot do, and how Arbitrica, a personal AI agent that lives in your browser, does the search for you at checkout.

## Why the same Booking.com hotel can cost less from another country

A hotel does not sell through one single channel. It distributes its inventory through Booking.com, Expedia, wholesalers, local travel agencies and its own website, often under separate agreements for separate markets. Some rates and allotments are set aside for travelers in a given country, and many promotions only run in specific countries. Searching from another country opens up that country's inventory, channels, local rates and promotions, and some of them are cheaper than anything available from your own country.

So the price you see from your own country is one slice of what exists for that hotel. The same hotel, on the same dates and with the same cancellation policy, can be cheaper when the search is made from a different country, often at a different seller. The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper elsewhere.

A real example: Booking.com offered one hotel stay for $1,527.39. Arbitrica found the identical hotel and dates for $1,180.27, with all taxes and fees included. That earned the user $347.12, or 23%.

## What changes when you search from another country

Several things can be different for a search made from another country:

- **Inventory.** Hotels give allotments to partners who sell mainly in one market, so some availability only shows up for searches from that country.

- **Channels.** Local booking sites, travel agencies and wholesalers often sell in only a few countries.

- **Local rates.** Some rates are negotiated for a specific market, such as domestic travelers.

- **Promotions.** Seasonal sales, mobile deals and campaigns are often limited to one or a few countries.

- **How the total is shown.** Some countries show prices with taxes and fees included, others add them at the end, so only the final total is a fair comparison.

> Chart: Different countries get different inventory, channels, local rates, promotions and currencies, and pricing algorithms move rates all day.

The cheapest country changes from hotel to hotel and from day to day. There is no single country you can always pick. Independent research points the same way: a 2024 NordVPN study found that travel bookings made through US websites came out up to 70% higher than through websites elsewhere (its largest gap was a car rental). In one case, a seven-night stay in a triple room at a Milan hotel for a family of three cost about $1,216 searched from the US and $1,012 searched from Italy.

> Chart: 2024 NordVPN study: a seven-night stay in a triple room at a Milan hotel for a family of three cost about $1,216 searched from the US and $1,012 searched from Italy.

## Can a VPN get you the lower price?

Sometimes, but slowly. A VPN lets you search from one other country at a time. You connect to a server, reload the hotel page, check the final total, and repeat for the next country. With 195 countries, doing that for every hotel you consider is not realistic.

The common problems with the VPN route:

- **One country per try.** Each country takes a few minutes once you clear cookies, reload and get to the final total.

- **No way to know where to look.** The cheapest country for one hotel is often not the cheapest for the next one.

- **Detection.** Many websites recognize traffic from well-known commercial VPN servers, and the results you get may not match what a traveler in that country sees.

- **Totals that mislead.** A lower headline price can end up higher once taxes, fees and currency conversion are added.

- **Rate conditions.** Some local rates come with conditions such as residency. Read them before you book.

If you tried a VPN and saw no difference, that is common. The country you picked may not have a better rate for that hotel, or the VPN server may have been recognized. For a side-by-side view, see [VPN vs. Arbitrica for hotel booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/vpn-vs-arbitrica-hotel-booking.html).

### If you try it by hand

- **Fix the hotel and dates**Write down your baseline total with taxes and fees, the cancellation terms and the meal plan.

- **Use a private window**Log out of booking accounts so member prices do not mix into the comparison.

- **Check one country at a time**Record the final total, not the headline rate, and note who is selling it.

- **Read the rate conditions**Look for residency rules and check your card's foreign transaction fee before paying.

## Is it legal to book a hotel at another country's price?

Booking a published rate is an ordinary consumer purchase, and prices that differ by market are common in travel. What matters is the conditions of the specific rate: if a rate is restricted to residents of one country and you are not one, the hotel can refuse it. This is general information, not legal advice.

In Europe, regulators have looked closely at the contracts between Booking.com and hotels. In July 2024, Spain's competition authority (CNMC) fined Booking.com about €413 million for abusing its dominant position in the Spanish hotel market. In September 2024, the Court of Justice of the EU ruled in Case C-264/23 (Booking.com v 25hours Hotel Company Berlin) that price parity clauses in contracts between Booking.com and hotels cannot simply be treated as ancillary restraints that fall outside EU competition rules.

## What about booking site terms of service?

Booking site terms mostly target things like automated scraping for resale, payment fraud and abuse of cancellation policies. Finding a published rate for the same hotel and booking it yourself, with your own card and under the rate's own conditions, is a normal booking. Arbitrica prepares the booking for the identical hotel, and you review and pay yourself.

## How Arbitrica finds the lowest price automatically

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that meets you at the checkout when you are about to pay. It searches the same hotel from 195 countries and finds the lowest price on Earth for it, at a different seller from the one you are on. It validates that the lower price is for the identical hotel and includes all taxes and fees, checks that the price will not suddenly change, and then prepares the booking so you only review and pay.

> Chart: By hand, a VPN checks one country at a time. Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries at once.

That search at checkout is live arbitrage. Prices also move over time, which is where multiple-time arbitrage comes in. Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after you book, until the free-cancellation window ends. When it finds the identical hotel for less, the mechanism prepares a re-booking at the lower price, and the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled.

Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year. The same mechanisms are not limited to hotels. Searching from other countries and repeating the search inside a cancellation or return window also works for flights, car rentals, event tickets, online shopping such as Amazon, and subscriptions. Companies use the same approach for teams traveling to trade shows and conferences.

## Manual VPN search vs. Arbitrica

| Dimension | VPN, by hand | Arbitrica |

| Countries checked | One at a time | The same hotel from 195 countries |

| Who does the work | You | Arbitrica, at checkout |

| Identical hotel check | You compare details yourself | Validated, including all taxes and fees |

| After you book | Nothing | The approach repeats the search until free cancellation ends |

| Beyond hotels | Manual every time | Flights, car rentals, event tickets, online shopping |

For the wider picture, see [why Booking.com prices differ by country](https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-prices-different-countries.html) and [whether there is a cheapest country to book hotels from](https://arbitrica.com/blog/cheapest-country-to-book-hotels-from.html).

## Frequently asked questions

### Does this also happen on Expedia, Hotels.com and Agoda?

Yes. Prices for the same hotel differ by country on most large booking sites, not only Booking.com. Arbitrica searches the same hotel no matter who sells it, and the lowest price it finds is at a different seller from the one you are on.

### Will the hotel honor the cheaper rate when I arrive?

A booking at a lower rate is a normal reservation with a normal confirmation number. Read the rate conditions before you pay. If a rate is limited to residents of a specific country, the hotel can ask for proof at check-in.

### What about chains like Marriott or Hilton?

Chain hotels also sell through many channels and run country-specific rates and promotions, so the same hotel can cost different amounts depending on the country you search from. Arbitrica looks for the lowest price for the identical hotel whoever sells it.

### Can the hotel cancel a booking made at another country's rate?

If you meet the conditions of the rate, it is a normal confirmed booking. The risk comes from rates with conditions you do not meet, such as residents-only rates, so check them before paying.

### How much can searching from other countries earn me?

A real example: Booking.com offered one hotel stay for $1,527.39. Arbitrica found the identical hotel and dates for $1,180.27, with all taxes and fees included. That earned the user $347.12, or 23%.

# Booking.com price match: how it works (and the better alternative)

The guarantee refunds a difference you find and prove yourself. Getting the lower price before you pay is simpler.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-price-match.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Save money

## Key takeaways

- Booking.com's price match refunds the difference only for a public, bookable lower price with exactly the same conditions.
- Claims often fail on a different cancellation policy, room type, member-only price or a missed deadline.
- The guarantee does nothing to help you find lower prices available from other countries.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout and prepares the booking at a different seller, so there is nothing to claim.
- If you already booked a refundable rate, rebook at the lower price and cancel the original only after the new booking is confirmed.

Booking.com's price match guarantee is real but narrow. It covers a lower price you find yourself on another public site, for a booking with exactly the same conditions, and you have to file a claim. The better route is to get the lower price before you pay. This page explains how the guarantee works, why so many claims fail, and how Arbitrica, a personal AI agent, finds the lowest price for the same hotel at checkout.

## Does Booking.com have a price match guarantee?

Yes. Booking.com's "We Price Match" promise says that if you find the same booking cheaper on another website, Booking.com will refund the difference. The lower price has to be for the same hotel and the same dates. It also has to be for the same room type, with the same cancellation and booking conditions, and it has to be publicly bookable. Claims go through Booking.com customer service and must be made within the deadline in Booking.com's terms, so check the current terms for your reservation.

## How to claim Booking.com's price match

Find the lower total price on a public site, document it, and send it to Booking.com customer service before the deadline.

- **Find the lower price on a public site**It has to be bookable, not just listed.

- **Confirm it is the same booking**Same hotel on the same dates. The room type, cancellation policy and extras such as breakfast have to match too.

- **Take a screenshot**Show the URL, the date and the final total with taxes and fees.

- **Contact customer service**Use your reservation or the help center, and include your booking number, the link to the lower price and the screenshot.

- **Wait for the review**If the claim is approved, Booking.com refunds the difference.

## Why many Booking.com price match claims are rejected

Booking.com's definition of "the same booking" is stricter than most travelers expect. The usual reasons a claim fails:

- The cheaper rate has a different cancellation policy.

- It is the same hotel, but the room type, board or occupancy does not match exactly.

- The cheaper price is a member, loyalty, app-only or coupon price, which does not count as public.

- The claim is filed after the deadline.

- The price changed by the time Booking.com checked it.

- The two totals are not comparable because taxes and fees are shown differently.

TipCapture the lower price with taxes and fees visible on the final step before payment. A screenshot of a search results page rarely proves the total.

## A better way than claiming a price match

Get the lower price before you pay instead of claiming a refund afterward. Different countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions, so searching the same hotel from another country can open up prices you cannot get from your own country. The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when it is searched from the right country.

Finding that country by hand means one VPN connection at a time, and checking all 195 countries is impossible in practice. Arbitrica does it for you at checkout. It searches the same hotel from 195 countries, finds the lowest price on Earth for it at a different seller from the one you are on, and prepares the booking so you only review and pay.

> Chart: At checkout Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries, checks it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price.

A real example: Booking.com offered one hotel stay for $1,527.39. Arbitrica found the identical hotel and dates for $1,180.27, with all taxes and fees included. That earned the user $347.12, or 23%. Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

> Chart: A real booking: offered at $1,527.39, found for $1,180.27 for the identical hotel. Arbitrica earned the user $347.12 (23%).

## Why the price match misses prices from other countries

The guarantee only works on a lower price you have already found and documented, and most travelers only search from their own country. It does nothing to help you find the inventory, local rates and promotions that open up when the same hotel is searched from another country, and that is often where the bigger gaps are. In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country. Arbitrica starts from those prices instead of waiting for you to find one. More on where the gaps come from is in [why Booking.com prices differ by country](https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-prices-different-countries.html).

## Booking.com price match vs. Arbitrica

| Dimension | Booking.com price match | Arbitrica |

| Who searches | You, by hand | Arbitrica, at checkout |

| Where it looks | Sites you check from your own country | The same hotel from 195 countries, at other sellers |

| When you get the lower price | After booking, if a claim is approved | Before you pay (live arbitrage) |

| Identical booking check | Booking.com reviews your evidence | Validates the identical hotel, including all taxes and fees, and checks the price will not suddenly change |

| Effort | Screenshots and a claim | Arbitrica prepares the booking, you review and pay |

| After you book | Only a price you find and claim yourself | The approach repeats the search until free cancellation ends (multiple-time arbitrage) |

| Beyond hotels | Booking.com stays only | Flights, car rentals, event tickets, online shopping |

## What if you have already booked and the price dropped?

If the lower price is on another public site and you are within the claim deadline, file the price match claim. If your rate has free cancellation, you can also book the lower price and cancel the original before the cancellation deadline. Book the new one first and cancel second, so you are never left without a hotel.

This is the idea behind multiple-time arbitrage. Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after you book, until the free-cancellation window ends. When it finds the identical hotel for less, the mechanism prepares a re-booking at the lower price, and the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled. Read more in [what to do when a hotel price drops after booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hotel-price-drop-after-booking.html) and [how to rebook a hotel at a lower price](https://arbitrica.com/blog/rebook-hotel-at-lower-price.html).

> Chart: Multiple-time arbitrage: the search repeats after a refundable booking. The new booking is confirmed first; only then is the original cancelled.

The same approach works beyond hotels: flights, car rentals, event tickets, pre-orders in online shopping and anything else with a cancellation or return window. Companies that book teams into trade shows and conferences can use it in the same way.

## Price match or search first: a quick decision guide

- **You have not paid yet:** search the same hotel from other countries first. There is nothing to claim if you book the lower price from the start.

- **You already booked and found a lower public price with identical terms:** file the price match claim before the deadline.

- **You booked a refundable rate and the price fell anywhere:** rebook at the lower price, and cancel only after the new booking is confirmed.

- **You booked a non-refundable rate:** the price match is your only route, and only against an offer with the same non-refundable conditions.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Booking.com price match work for non-refundable bookings?

The cheaper offer has to have the same conditions as your booking. A non-refundable booking can only be matched against an offer with the same non-refundable conditions. Check Booking.com's current terms for your reservation.

### What sites count as "public" for a price match claim?

A booking site that anyone can reach without a login, member account or coupon code. Loyalty rates, member-only prices and coupon-gated prices do not qualify. Other major booking sites such as Expedia, Hotels.com and Agoda do.

### Does the price match help me find prices from other countries?

No. The guarantee depends on a lower price you find and document yourself. Arbitrica works the other way around: it searches the same hotel from 195 countries before you pay, so you book the lower price from the start and there is nothing to claim.

### What is the easiest way to pay less than the Booking.com price?

Use Arbitrica at checkout. It searches the same hotel from 195 countries, validates that the lower price is for the identical hotel with all taxes and fees included, and prepares the booking at a different seller for you to review and pay.

# Booking.com price tracker: how to track a hotel price and when it is not enough

Price alerts tell you when one listing drops. The lower price for the same hotel is often somewhere a tracker never looks.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-price-tracker.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Save money

## Key takeaways

- A Booking.com price tracker watches one listing over time and alerts you when its price drops.
- To track by hand, fix the exact search, keep your sign-in state the same and record the total with taxes and fees.
- Google added individual hotel price tracking with email alerts to Google Hotels in April 2026.
- Trackers do not search the same hotel from other countries, where 80% of countries showed a lower price in a test of 1,000 hotels.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout and repeats the search after booking until free cancellation ends.

A Booking.com price tracker watches the price of a hotel you are interested in, or one you have already booked, and tells you when it drops. That is useful, because Booking.com prices move all the time. But a tracker only watches one listing, on one site, as seen from one country, and the lower price you are looking for is often somewhere it never checks.

## Why Booking.com hotel prices change

The price you see for a hotel on Booking.com is set by the hotel's revenue management system and the deals it runs on the platform. It reacts to how fast rooms are selling, what nearby hotels charge, events in the city and the number of days left before arrival. The same stay can be priced several times between the day you first look and the day you check in.

> Chart: Illustrative: revenue management moves the price of the same stay as arrival approaches.

Some of the difference is also about who is looking. Booking.com's Genius loyalty program gives signed-in members discounts at participating properties, so a price checked while signed in can differ from one checked while signed out. If you track a price, keep the conditions the same every time, or you will be measuring your own settings instead of the hotel's rate.

## How to track a Booking.com price by hand

You do not need any software to track one hotel. You need a consistent method and a few minutes every couple of days.

- **Fix the exact search**Same hotel, check-in and check-out dates, number of adults and children, room type, meal plan and cancellation terms.

- **Keep your sign-in state the same**Check either signed in or signed out every time, so Genius discounts do not distort the record.

- **Record the total, not the nightly rate**Go far enough into the booking flow to see the final amount with taxes and fees, and write it down with the date.

- **Check at a regular rhythm**Every two or three days is enough for most trips; more often in the last week before free cancellation ends.

- **Act on a real drop**If the total falls for the identical stay and your booking is refundable, rebook first and cancel the original only after the new booking is confirmed.

A simple spreadsheet with one row per check is the best price history you can get for a specific stay. It also shows you how much the price moves, which tells you whether waiting is worth it.

## Booking.com price drop alerts and tracking tools

If checking by hand sounds like work, several kinds of tools will watch prices for you. They fall into three groups.

### Search engine price tracking

Google added individual hotel price tracking to Google Hotels in April 2026, according to 9to5Google. On a hotel's page you can switch on "Track this hotel" for your dates and receive email alerts when the price changes. At launch it was available to signed-in users in English and Spanish. It watches the prices Google shows for that hotel, which makes it a good starting point before you book.

### Post-booking trackers

Post-booking trackers watch a reservation you already have and alert you when the rate falls. RoomHawk, for example, says it tracks your booking automatically and monitors more than 2 million rooms. Pruvo, one of the early names in this space, now focuses on business customers. Services in this group differ in how you add a booking, how often they check and whether they help with the rebooking itself, so read each one's own description before you rely on it.

### Browser add-ons

Some browser extensions add a price history or a price-drop alert to Booking.com pages. They are convenient for watching one listing over time while you decide.

For a wider look at the category, see the guide to the [best hotel price trackers of 2026](https://arbitrica.com/blog/best-hotel-price-trackers-2026.html) and the overview of [hotel price trackers](https://arbitrica.com/hotel-price-tracker.html).

## What a hotel price tracker can and cannot do

| A tracker can | A tracker cannot |

| Tell you when the price of a listing you watch goes down | Find prices from countries it does not search from |

| Save you from checking every day | Guarantee that the price in an alert is still available when you click |

| Show how much a price moves over time | Confirm that the cheaper offer has the same room, inclusions and cancellation terms |

| Prompt you to rebook before free cancellation ends | Help with a non-refundable booking, which cannot be rebooked without a loss |

The biggest gap is the first one. A tracker watches movement over time. It does not answer a different question: is the same hotel, on the same dates, available at a lower price right now from somewhere else?

## Rebooking after a Booking.com price drop

An alert only becomes money if you can act on it. With a free cancellation booking, you can book the identical stay at the lower total, wait for the confirmation and then cancel the original before the deadline. The new booking does not have to be on Booking.com; the identical hotel may be lower at another site or at the hotel's own website. Make sure the room type, meal plan and cancellation terms match before you cancel anything. The full process is in the guide to [rebooking a hotel at a lower price](https://arbitrica.com/blog/rebook-hotel-at-lower-price.html).

If you found a lower price elsewhere before your stay, Booking.com's own price match policy may also apply. The article on the [Booking.com price match](https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-price-match.html) explains how it works and where it falls short.

## Where trackers stop: the same hotel from other countries

Every tracker described above checks prices from one place. Yet the same hotel, on the same dates, can be offered at different prices depending on which country you search from. Different countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions, so searching the same hotel from another country can open up lower prices you cannot get from your own country.

In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, and the typical gap was 20-40%. That kind of difference exists at the same moment, so no amount of waiting for a drop on one listing will find it. The article on [Booking.com prices in different countries](https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-prices-different-countries.html) explains this in detail.

> Chart: Geographic arbitrage (other countries, at checkout) and time arbitrage (later moments, after you pay).

## How Arbitrica goes further than a price tracker

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that meets you at checkout. When you are about to pay for a hotel on Booking.com, it searches the same hotel from 195 countries, validates that it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price on Earth. The lower price it finds is always at a different provider than the one you are on. You review and pay.

> Chart: A real booking: offered at $1,527.39, found for $1,180.27 for the identical hotel. Arbitrica earned the user $347.12 (23%).

In one real booking, a hotel was offered at $1,527.39 on Booking.com. Arbitrica found the identical hotel for $1,180.27, earning the user $347.12, or 23%.

Time still matters after you book. Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after you book, until free cancellation ends. When the identical hotel becomes available at a lower total, a new booking is prepared and confirmed first, and only then is the original cancelled. That covers both kinds of saving a tracker is built for and the larger one it cannot see.

Companies get the same benefit at scale. Travel managers and operations managers booking teams into trade show or conference cities can use the same approach on every booking, instead of asking each traveler to set up alerts. The mechanisms also work beyond hotels, for flights, event tickets and online shopping.

## A practical setup for your next booking

- **Book a refundable rate**A tracker or a repeat search is only useful if you can still change the booking.

- **Search from other countries before you pay**The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper elsewhere, and the gap between countries is usually larger than a drop over time.

- **Turn on one tracker**Google's hotel tracking or a post-booking tracker is enough; several alerts for the same stay add noise.

- **Check identical terms**Same hotel, room, inclusions and cancellation terms, compared on the full total.

- **Confirm before you cancel**The new booking must be confirmed before the original is cancelled.

Research demonstrated that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I track a Booking.com hotel price?

Yes. You can record the total for the same search every few days, turn on hotel price tracking in Google Hotels, or use a post-booking tracker that alerts you when the rate drops.

### What should I do when a Booking.com price drops after I book?

If your booking has free cancellation, book the identical stay at the lower total, wait for the confirmation, then cancel the original before the deadline.

### Why do I see different Booking.com prices when I check again?

Hotel prices change with demand and occupancy, and signed-in Genius members can see discounts at participating properties. Keep the same search and sign-in state each time you check.

### Can a price tracker find the lowest price for a hotel?

Not on its own. A tracker watches one listing over time from one place. The same hotel searched from other countries can be lower at the same moment, which a tracker does not check.

# Why Booking.com prices differ by country

The same hotel on the same dates can cost less searched from another country. Here is why, how big the gap is, and how to book it safely.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-prices-different-countries.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Hidden prices

## Key takeaways

- Hotels sell through many channels under market-by-market agreements, so different countries get different inventory, local rates and promotions.
- The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when searched from another country.
- In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own.
- Compare the final total, cancellation policy, meal plan and rate conditions before booking from another country.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout and prepares the booking at the lowest price on Earth.

Booking.com is the world's largest hotel booking platform, with millions of properties listed. What most travelers do not realize is that the same hotel, on the same dates, can cost less when it is searched from another country. A stay at [The Savoy, London](https://sovrn.co/zr0beu5), for example, can be priced differently depending on the country it is searched from. Knowing why makes it much easier to stop overpaying.

## How prices for the same hotel differ by country

A hotel sells through many channels at once: Booking.com, other booking sites, wholesalers, local travel agencies and its own website. Many of those agreements are made market by market. Different countries therefore get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions, and searching the same hotel from another country can open up prices you cannot get from your own country.

The main reasons a search from another country can come back lower:

- **Market rates.** Hotels and their partners agree rates for specific markets.

- **Local and domestic rates.** Some rates are meant for travelers in one country.

- **Promotions.** Seasonal sales, loyalty deals and campaigns often run in only some countries. A deal visible in Germany may not appear in the United States.

- **Local sellers.** Some booking sites and agencies sell in only a few countries, with their own allotments.

- **How totals are shown.** Taxes and fees are included up front in some countries and added at the end in others, so always compare the final total.

> Chart: Different countries get different inventory, channels, local rates, promotions and currencies, and pricing algorithms move rates all day.

## How big are the differences?

For the same hotel and dates, the price found from the right country is often 5-30% below the price offered from your own country. On a long or expensive stay that adds up fast.

In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, and the typical gap was 20-40%. Independent research found the same pattern: a 2024 NordVPN study found that travel bookings made through US websites came out up to 70% higher than through websites elsewhere (its largest gap was a car rental). In one case, a seven-night stay in a triple room at a Milan hotel for a family of three cost about $1,216 searched from the US and $1,012 searched from Italy.

> Chart: In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler’s own country. The typical gap was 20–40%.

A real example: Booking.com offered one hotel stay for $1,527.39. Arbitrica found the identical hotel and dates for $1,180.27, with all taxes and fees included. That earned the user $347.12, or 23%.

## Why hotels and booking sites work this way

Demand and purchasing power vary a lot between countries. Selling through partners and promotions that target each market lets hotels fill more of their inventory without lowering their rate everywhere. It is standard practice across the industry, not just at Booking.com: Expedia, Hotels.com, Agoda and Trip.com all sell the same hotels through many markets and channels.

There is also a timing layer on top. Hotel revenue-management systems move rates as occupancy and demand change, so the gap between countries is not fixed either. A country that is lowest for a hotel this week may not be lowest next week. For more on that, see [how hotel dynamic pricing works](https://arbitrica.com/blog/how-hotel-dynamic-pricing-works.html).

## Can you get the lower prices?

Often, yes. Many of these are real, bookable rates. Check the conditions before you pay: some local rates are limited to residents of a country, and the hotel can ask for proof at check-in.

The hard part is knowing which country has the lowest price for a specific hotel. It changes with demand, promotions and inventory. A hotel that is lowest when searched from Thailand today may be lowest from Brazil tomorrow. Checking with a VPN means one country at a time, and searching all 195 countries by hand is impossible in practice. See [Booking.com different prices and VPNs, explained](https://arbitrica.com/blog/booking-com-different-prices-vpn-explained.html) and [VPN vs. Arbitrica](https://arbitrica.com/blog/vpn-vs-arbitrica-hotel-booking.html) for the details.

## What to compare before you book from another country

A lower number is only a saving when everything else matches. Before you pay, line up these details for both offers:

| Detail | Why it matters |

| Hotel name and address | Similar names can belong to different properties. |

| Dates and guests | A change of one night or one guest resets the price. |

| Cancellation policy | A non-refundable rate is often lower, but removes your option to rebook. |

| Meal plan | Breakfast included on one offer and not the other can explain the gap. |

| Final total | Taxes, city tax and resort fees decide the real price. |

| Currency and card fees | A foreign-currency payment can add a card fee to the total. |

| Rate conditions | Residents-only rates can be refused at check-in. |

TipIf your card offers to charge you in your own currency at checkout, compare that amount with the local-currency total. The conversion rate offered at checkout is often worse than your card's own rate.

## Common myths about booking from another country

- **"One country is always cheapest."** The lowest country changes with the hotel, the dates, promotions and inventory. A rule that worked for one trip rarely holds for the next.

- **"Switching my connection reprices the hotel."** The difference comes from the inventory, sellers, local rates and promotions another country has access to, not from a booking site changing the same listing for you.

- **"A lower headline rate means a lower price."** Taxes and fees are shown differently in different countries. Only the final total counts.

- **"Rates from another country are not real."** Many are ordinary bookable rates with normal confirmations. The exception is a rate limited to residents, which the hotel can refuse if you do not qualify.

Keeping these in mind saves time: you stop chasing a magic country and start comparing like for like.

## How Arbitrica finds the lowest price

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that meets you at the checkout when you are about to pay. It searches the same hotel from 195 countries and finds the lowest price on Earth for it, at a different seller from the one you are on. It validates that the lower price is for the identical hotel and includes all taxes and fees, checks that the price will not suddenly change, and then prepares the booking so you only review and pay.

Prices also change over time. Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after you book, until the free-cancellation window ends. When the identical hotel gets cheaper, the mechanism prepares a re-booking at the lower price, and the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled. Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

> Chart: 2024 NordVPN study: a seven-night stay in a triple room at a Milan hotel for a family of three cost about $1,216 searched from the US and $1,012 searched from Italy.

## For companies and frequent travelers

The gap between countries matters most where bookings repeat. Travel managers, operations managers and teams heading to trade shows and conferences book the same cities again and again, and every booking is another chance to pay more than necessary. Arbitrica serves companies as well as individual travelers, with the same search from 195 countries at checkout. See [business travel hotel savings](https://arbitrica.com/blog/business-travel-hotel-savings.html).

## Beyond hotels

The same mechanisms work beyond hotels, for flights, car rentals, event tickets and online shopping such as Amazon. Different countries get different inventory, sellers and promotions for those too, and anything with a cancellation or return window can be searched again after you buy.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why does the same hotel cost less from another country?

Hotels and their partners agree rates, allotments and promotions market by market, so each country gets access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions. Some of those are lower than what you can get from your own country.

### Is it legal to book a hotel at another country's price?

Booking a published rate is an ordinary purchase. Check the rate conditions, because some local rates are limited to residents and the hotel can ask for proof at check-in.

### Which country is cheapest for Booking.com hotels?

No single country is always cheapest. The lowest country changes with the hotel, the dates, promotions and inventory, which is why checking many countries matters.

### Does this only happen on Booking.com?

No. Expedia, Hotels.com, Agoda and Trip.com also sell the same hotels through many markets and channels, so prices for the same hotel differ by country there too.

# Business travel hotel savings for travel managers

Negotiated rates cover one market. The same hotel is often cheaper from another country, and that saving needs no change of hotel or policy.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/business-travel-hotel-savings.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: For companies

## Key takeaways

- GBTA projected global business travel spending of about $1.48 trillion in 2024, with lodging one of the biggest line items.
- A negotiated corporate rate covers one market and says nothing about prices for the same hotel from other countries.
- The same hotel is often 5-30% cheaper when searched from another country, sometimes below a corporate rate.
- Arbitrica keeps the traveler in the hotel they chose, on the same dates and terms; only the price changes.
- In Arbitrica's rebooking flow the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled, so no traveler is left without a hotel.

Hotels are one of the largest controllable costs in a business travel program, and one of the least examined. Companies negotiate rates, set nightly caps and steer travelers toward preferred channels, yet the same hotel on the same dates is often 5-30% cheaper when it is searched from another country. That gap sits outside most travel policies, and it can be captured without changing which hotel a traveler stays in.

This article is for the people who carry hotel spend inside a company: travel managers who run the program, operations managers who book travel for staff, and teams heading to trade shows and conferences. Arbitrica serves companies as well as individual travelers, and the approach below works for both.

## The scale of business travel hotel spend

The Global Business Travel Association (GBTA) projected global business travel spending of about $1.48 trillion in 2024, and lodging is one of the biggest line items in that total. For a single company the numbers add up quickly. Take a company with 150 traveling employees who each spend 40 nights a year in hotels at an average of $220 a night: that is 6,000 hotel nights and $1.32 million in annual hotel spend.

At the low end of the typical spread, a price 5% lower for the identical hotel is worth $66,000 a year to that company. At 15%, it is worth $198,000.

> Chart: The same item, with the same dates and terms, is often 5–30% cheaper bought from another country or at another moment.

## Why negotiated corporate hotel rates leave money on the table

Travel management companies (TMCs) and corporate travel teams negotiate rates with hotel chains, usually as a discount off the best available rate. Those agreements are valuable, but they cover only one part of hotel pricing. A negotiated rate is set for one market, normally the company's own country, and it says nothing about the prices available for the same hotel from other countries.

Different countries get access to different inventory, distribution channels, local rates and promotions. Searching the same hotel from another country can therefore open up prices that are not available from your own country, sometimes below a negotiated corporate rate. In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country.

### An illustrative example

Say a London hotel shows a public rate of $250 a night from the United States and your negotiated corporate rate is $220. That looks like a solid 12% discount. If the same hotel, for the same dates and conditions, comes up at $185 a night when searched from another country, the corporate rate is no longer the best price available to your traveler.

| Price for the same London hotel | Per night | Difference vs. public rate |

| Public rate from the United States | $250 | Baseline |

| Negotiated corporate rate | $220 | 12% lower |

| Price found from another country | $185 | 26% lower |

These figures are illustrative. The actual spread depends on the hotel, the dates and the countries searched, and it changes over time.

## Why doing this by hand does not scale

A traveler with a VPN can switch to another country and search again, one country at a time. Doing that for 195 countries on every trip, while checking that each result is the identical hotel with all taxes and fees included, is impossible in practice. Travel managers cannot ask employees to spend hours on it, and spot checks from three or four countries miss most of the spread.

## How Arbitrica works for companies

Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser. When anyone in the company, a traveler or the person booking for them, reaches the checkout for a hotel, Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries and finds the lowest price on Earth for it, at a different seller from the one they are on. It validates that the lower price is for the identical hotel and includes all taxes and fees, checks that the price will not suddenly change, and then prepares the booking so the person booking only reviews and pays.

> Chart: At checkout Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries, checks it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price.

Two mechanisms work together:

- **Geographic arbitrage at checkout (live arbitrage):** the same hotel is searched from 195 countries in real time, before the traveler pays.

- **Multiple-time arbitrage:** hotel prices keep moving after booking. Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after the booking is made, until the free-cancellation window ends, and prepares a re-booking at the lower price. The new booking is confirmed before the original reservation is cancelled.

> Chart: Multiple-time arbitrage: the search repeats after a refundable booking. The new booking is confirmed first; only then is the original cancelled.

The same mechanisms apply beyond hotels. Flights, car rentals, event tickets and other purchases with a cancellation window can be searched from other countries and checked again over time.

## Who inside a company gets the most from it

### Travel managers

Travel managers own the hotel line in the budget and answer for it. Negotiated rates and caps set a ceiling, but they do not tell you whether the same hotel was available for less from another country on the day it was booked. Arbitrica searches every hotel at the checkout from 195 countries, so the price the company pays is the lowest it could find for the identical hotel, with all taxes and fees included. More in [hotel savings for travel managers](https://arbitrica.com/blog/travel-manager-hotel-savings.html).

### Operations managers

Operations managers and office managers often book hotels for colleagues, crews or visiting staff, many trips a month and usually under time pressure. Checking other countries by hand is out of the question at that volume. With Arbitrica, the search happens when they reach the checkout, and the lower-priced booking is prepared for them to review and pay. See [travel costs for operations managers](https://arbitrica.com/blog/operations-manager-travel-costs.html).

### Teams traveling to trade shows and conferences

Trade shows and conferences are where hotel spend concentrates. A company sends several people to the same city on the same dates, when demand near the venue is high and prices tend to rise. That is when searching the same hotel from 195 countries matters most: each booking is checked at the checkout, not only the first one. Event hotels are also often booked weeks or months ahead with free cancellation, which leaves a long window for the multiple-time approach to repeat the search before the trip. See [trade show hotel prices](https://arbitrica.com/blog/trade-show-hotel-prices.html).

## Travel policy and duty of care

Arbitrica looks for the identical hotel the traveler already chose. The dates, room type and cancellation terms stay the same, so the traveler stays where the policy says they should and duty of care is unaffected. The only thing that changes is the price.

Travel managers should still confirm how a re-booked reservation is recorded in their booking tool and expense process, and whether bookings made outside a preferred channel count toward volume commitments negotiated with a hotel chain.

## Practical points for travel and operations managers

- Arbitrica looks for the identical hotel, dates and terms the traveler chose, so no change of hotel is needed.

- A rate with free cancellation keeps the window open for the search to be repeated after booking.

- Re-bookings are prepared for review, and the new booking is confirmed before the original is cancelled, so the traveler is never left without a hotel.

- Comparisons always use the final total with taxes and fees, which is also the number finance sees on the expense report.

## What it can be worth

Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year. In one real booking, a hotel was offered on Booking.com for $1,527.39. Arbitrica found the identical hotel for $1,180.27 and earned the user $347.12, or 23%.

For a company, the value scales with the number of hotel nights booked. Multiply your annual hotel spend by a conservative spread for your main destinations and you have a reasonable estimate before running a pilot. Teams that travel to the same trade shows every year can run the same estimate per event.

## How to run a pilot

- **Pick a group**Choose a set of frequent travelers, or the team going to your next trade show or conference.

- **Set a baseline**Record what each booking would have cost through your usual channel, with taxes and fees.

- **Book through the checkout as usual**Let Arbitrica search the same hotel from 195 countries and prepare the lower-priced booking for review.

- **Compare after one quarter**The results show whether the same hotels are cheaper from other countries for your destinations, and by how much.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a hotel be cheaper than our negotiated corporate rate?

Yes. A negotiated rate is set for one market, and the same hotel searched from another country can sometimes come in lower for the same dates and conditions.

### Does Arbitrica change which hotel our travelers stay in?

No. Arbitrica looks for the identical hotel, dates and terms the traveler chose, so policy and duty of care are unaffected. Only the price changes.

### How does Arbitrica help teams going to trade shows?

Each booking is searched from 195 countries at checkout, and because event hotels are often booked early with free cancellation, Arbitrica's approach can repeat the search before the trip and prepare a re-booking at a lower price.

### What should travel managers check before using it?

How a re-booked reservation is recorded in your booking tool and expense process, and whether bookings outside a preferred channel count toward volume commitments with a hotel chain.

# Is it cheaper to buy from another country online?

Sometimes by a lot. What decides it is the total you pay once shipping, import taxes and card fees are added.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/buy-online-cheaper-from-another-country.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Online shopping

## Key takeaways

- Online prices differ by country because of taxes in the sticker price, local competition, inventory, currency and purchasing power.
- A lower sticker price abroad can become a loss once shipping, import duty, VAT and card fees are added.
- Amazon runs separate national stores with their own prices, sellers and promotions.
- Some subscriptions and game stores tie accounts to your country of residence, so buying elsewhere can break their terms.
- Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries at checkout, validates the total and prepares the purchase for you to review and pay.

Often, yes. Online prices are different in different countries, sometimes by a little and sometimes by a lot. Whether you actually come out ahead depends on what you are buying and on the total you pay once shipping, taxes and fees are added. This guide goes through the main categories, what is legitimate and practical, and what to check before you buy.

## Why online prices differ between countries

Geo pricing in e-commerce is normal. A store selling into many countries rarely uses one global price, for several reasons:

- **Taxes in the sticker price.** In the EU and the UK, consumer prices usually include VAT. In the US, the listed price usually excludes sales tax, which is added at checkout. The same product can look more expensive in Europe simply because tax is already in the number.

- **Local competition.** A product competing with strong local rivals is often priced lower in that market.

- **Distribution and inventory.** Different countries get access to different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions. A national store may have bought stock at a different cost or run its own sales calendar.

- **Currency.** Prices set in local currency drift as exchange rates move, and stores do not reprice every day.

- **Purchasing power.** Digital goods in particular are often priced lower in countries with lower average incomes.

> Chart: The same item, with the same dates and terms, is often 5–30% cheaper bought from another country or at another moment.

## Buying from another country, category by category

| Category | Why prices differ | What to watch |

| Electronics and retail | Local competition, stock, sales calendars, tax in the price | Shipping, import duty and VAT, warranty country, plugs and voltage, keyboard layout, returns |

| Streaming subscriptions | Country-specific plans and catalogs | Terms that tie the account to your country of residence, payment method checks |

| Software | Country-specific price lists | License terms, activation limited to one country, support in your language |

| Games | Country-specific pricing on digital stores | Keys and accounts locked to one country or area, store rules on changing country |

| Flights | Fares and promotions that differ by point of sale and currency | Card foreign transaction fees, fare rules, payment methods accepted |

| Hotels | Different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions by country | Taxes and fees at checkout, cancellation terms |

| Event tickets | Different sellers, fees and currencies | Delivery method, transfer rules, seat details |

### Electronics and physical goods

This is where people most often ask whether it is cheaper to buy from another country. The answer turns on landed cost. A laptop that is $90 lower on a foreign store can end up more expensive once international shipping, import duty and import VAT or GST are added, plus a currency conversion fee on your card. Warranty is the other trap: some manufacturers only honor warranty in the country of purchase, which means sending the product abroad if it fails. Check the manufacturer's warranty terms before you buy.

### Subscriptions and software

Streaming and software prices vary widely by country, and that is well documented. But many services tie your account to the country where you live and check your payment method and location. Signing up in another country can break those terms and lead to a suspended account. The legitimate wins here are usually local promotions in your own country, annual plans, and buying software from a reseller that is authorized to sell in your country.

### Games

Digital game stores commonly set different prices by country, and many restrict keys or purchases to the country or area they were sold in. Keys bought elsewhere may simply not activate. Treat very low prices from unofficial key sellers with suspicion.

### Flights

Airline fares can differ depending on the country the ticket is sold in and the currency you pay in. The gap is sometimes worth it, especially on long-haul routes. Watch for card fees on foreign currency and make sure the fare rules, such as changes and baggage, are the same as the fare you were comparing against.

## Amazon price in a different country: what actually happens

Amazon runs separate national stores, such as amazon.com, amazon.co.uk and amazon.de, each with its own prices, sellers and promotions. The same product can have a noticeably different price on two of them. Many items on these stores can ship internationally, and some show an estimate of import fees at checkout so you see more of the total before paying. Others do not ship to your country at all. More detail is in [Amazon prices in different countries](https://arbitrica.com/blog/amazon-prices-different-countries.html).

When you compare Amazon stores, line up the same thing:

- The exact same product, model number and variant.

- The same seller type: sold by Amazon or by a third-party seller.

- Shipping to your address, not to the store's home country.

- Import duty and taxes for your country.

- Your card's foreign transaction fee, if any.

- How returns work from abroad.

## A worked example of landed cost (illustrative)

Here is how the math tends to go. The numbers are made up to show the method, not real quotes.

| Cost line | Your own country's store | Foreign store |

| Item price | $640 | $540 |

| Shipping | $0 | $35 |

| Import duty and VAT | $0 (already included) | $60 |

| Card foreign transaction fee | $0 | $16 |

| Total | $640 | $651 |

A $100 gap on the sticker price turned into an $11 loss. Change one or two lines, such as a store that ships at no extra charge or a card with no foreign fees, and the same purchase could save you money. That is why the total is the only number that matters.

TipBefore you buy from a foreign store, add up item, shipping, import duty and taxes, and your card's foreign fee in one line. If the total is not clearly lower, the warranty and returns risk is rarely worth it.

## What is legitimate, and what is not

- **Legitimate:** buying a physical product from a store in another country and paying the import taxes your country charges.

- **Legitimate:** booking a hotel, flight or ticket at a price available from another country, as long as you meet the booking's terms.

- **Risky:** signing up for subscriptions or game stores in a country you do not live in, when the terms require residence.

- **Not legitimate:** under-declaring the value of goods at customs to avoid duty.

## How Arbitrica applies the same mechanism to online purchases

Doing all this by hand for one purchase is work. Doing it for 195 countries is not realistic. Arbitrica is a personal AI agent that lives in your browser and meets you at checkout when you are about to pay. It searches the same item from 195 countries, finds the lowest price on Earth for it at a different seller from the one you are on, and validates that it is the identical item and that the price includes all taxes and fees. Then it prepares the purchase. You review and pay.

> Chart: At checkout Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries, checks it is identical with all taxes and fees included, and prepares everything at the lowest price.

The same item is often 5-30% cheaper elsewhere, and research showed that people earn on average $34 per online purchase with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

> Chart: Research demonstrated average earnings of $47 per hotel booking, $34 per online purchase and $107 per event ticket purchase, and up to $3,000, $3,000 and $1,500 a year.

For Amazon purchases, that means the agent looks for the same product at a lower total from another seller than the one in your cart. For purchases that ship later, such as pre-orders, or that have a return or cancellation window, Arbitrica's time arbitrage approach repeats the search after you buy and prepares a re-purchase at the lower price while you can still cancel the original. The new purchase is confirmed before the original is cancelled. Arbitrica also serves companies, including operations and travel managers.

It started with hotels, where the gaps are well known. The [guide to geographic price arbitrage](https://arbitrica.com/blog/what-is-geographic-price-arbitrage.html) explains the idea, and [how it works](https://arbitrica.com/how-it-works.html) shows the full flow. The same mechanism also covers [event tickets](https://arbitrica.com/blog/event-ticket-price-drops.html), and [AI shopping agents](https://arbitrica.com/blog/ai-shopping-agent-lowest-price.html) explains how an agent can do the searching for you.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is it cheaper to buy from another country online?

Often, but not always. The sticker price can be lower abroad while shipping, import duty, taxes and card fees make the total higher. Compare the full total for the identical item.

### Why are online prices different in different countries?

Taxes included or excluded in the listed price, local competition, different inventory, channels and promotions, currency movements and purchasing power all lead stores to price the same item differently by country.

### Is the Amazon price different in another country?

Yes. Amazon runs separate national stores with their own prices, sellers and promotions, so the same product can cost more or less on each one.

### What should I watch for when buying from abroad?

Shipping, import duty and VAT, warranty terms, plug and voltage differences, card foreign transaction fees, returns from abroad, and any terms that tie digital services to your country of residence.

### Does Arbitrica work for online shopping, not only hotels?

Yes. Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries at checkout, including Amazon purchases, validates it with all taxes and fees, and prepares the purchase for you to review and pay.

# Is there a cheapest country to book hotels from?

Lists of "best countries" go out of date fast. The country with the lowest price changes with the hotel, the dates and the seller.

Source: https://arbitrica.com/blog/cheapest-country-to-book-hotels-from.html  
Updated: 2026-10-25  
Topic: Hidden prices

## Key takeaways

- No single country is always cheapest for hotels; the winner changes with the hotel, the dates and the seller.
- In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own, with a typical gap of 20-40%.
- Lists that rank countries by income mislead, because promotions, sellers and exchange rates do not follow income.
- Always compare the final total, cancellation terms, meal plan and residency conditions before booking from another country.
- Arbitrica searches the same hotel from 195 countries at checkout, because the only reliable method is to check every country every time.

Search for the cheapest country to book hotels from and you will find confident lists: book from India, book from Thailand, book from Turkey. They are tidy, and they point at something real. The same hotel often has a different price in a different country. What does not exist is one country that wins every time.

This guide explains why the answer changes from hotel to hotel and from date to date, what actually makes a booking cheaper when it is made from another country, and how to find the lowest price without spending an evening switching VPN servers.

## The short answer: there is no single cheapest country

The country that gives the lowest price for a hotel in Lisbon in May may not be the one that wins for the same hotel in October, and it may lose again for a hotel two streets away. Three things decide it:

- **The hotel.** Each hotel decides which markets get promotions, which agencies and wholesalers sell its stays, and which local rates it loads. A large chain and an independent guesthouse make very different choices.

- **The dates.** A promotion aimed at one country may run for two weeks and then stop. Inventory given to a partner in one market can sell out while the hotel still has availability elsewhere.

- **The seller.** The same hotel can be sold by Booking.com, Expedia, the hotel's own website, a local agency in another country and several wholesale partners. Which of them is active in a given country, and at what price, varies.

So the useful answer to "which country should I book from" is: it depends on the hotel, the dates and who sells it in that country, and you only find out by checking.

> Chart: In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler’s own country. The typical gap was 20–40%.

In a test of 1,000 hotels searched from 100 countries, 80% of countries showed a lower price than the traveler's own country, and the typical gap was 20-40%. Lower prices are common; the country that has them is what keeps changing.

## Why the same hotel has a different price in a different country

When you search the same hotel from another country, you get access to a different set of offers. Different countries see different inventory, channels, local rates and promotions. A few mechanisms do most of the work.

> Chart: Different countries get different inventory, channels, local rates, promotions and currencies, and pricing algorithms move rates all day.

### Market-targeted rates and promotions

Hotels can create rates that are offered only to travelers booking from particular countries. A resort that wants more guests from a market it is trying to grow might run a discount there and nowhere else. These rates are real, bookable and honored at check-in. They come and go with the hotel's sales plans, which is one reason any list of "best countries" goes out of date quickly.

### Different sellers in different countries

The big booking sites operate almost everywhere, but they are not the only sellers. In many countries, local online agencies, tour operators and bank or airline travel portals also sell hotel stays, often from inventory that wholesalers bought in bulk at negotiated rates. Searching from another country can put you in front of a seller you would never see from your own country, sometimes with a lower price for the identical hotel and dates.

### Local currency and tax display

Some rates are set in a local currency and not adjusted every time the exchange rate moves, so a currency swing can make one country's price lower for a while. How taxes appear also differs. In the United States, hotel prices were long shown before taxes and resort fees; the Federal Trade Commission's fee rule, in force since May 2025, now requires mandatory fees to be included in the advertised price, though government taxes can still be listed separately. Much of Europe shows tax-inclusive totals. A price that looks lower may simply be missing something, so a fair check always compares the final total.

### Member and app pricing

Member discounts, loyalty tiers and app-only rates are not rolled out the same way in every market. A logged-in discount you get in one country may not exist in another, and the reverse is also true. When you test prices, note whether you are logged in, because it changes what you are comparing.

For a deeper look at how these differences fit together, see the guide to [geographic price arbitrage](https://arbitrica.com/blog/what-is-geographic-price-arbitrage.html) and the wider explainer on [hidden hotel prices](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hidden-hotel-prices-guide.html).

## Why "book from a cheaper country" lists mislead

Most lists rank countries by average income, on the theory that hotels charge less where people earn less. Sometimes that holds. Often it does not:

- Promotions do not follow income. A hotel targeting a wealthy market with a launch discount can make that market the lowest for a month.

- Some lower-income markets have fewer sellers, so the hotel's best offer may not appear there at all.

- Some rates are restricted to residents, and the hotel can ask for proof at check-in. A rate you cannot use is not a saving.

- Exchange rates move every day, which reshuffles the order without anyone changing a price.

The pattern you can rely on is narrower and more useful: the same hotel is often 5 to 30 percent cheaper when booked from somewhere else, and the somewhere else keeps changing. Independent research agrees that the gaps can be large: a 2024 NordVPN study found that travel bookings made through US websites came out up to 70% higher than through websites elsewhere (its largest gap was a car rental).

## What changes from country to country, and what to check

| Factor | What can differ by country | What to check before you book |

| Seller | Global sites, local agencies, wholesalers, the hotel's own site | That the seller is reputable and the booking confirmation names the hotel |

| Rate type | Refundable, non-refundable, breakfast included or not | That you are comparing the same cancellation terms and meal plan |

| Taxes and fees | Shown upfront, added at checkout, or paid at the hotel | The final total, including city tax and resort fees |

| Currency | Price set in local currency or converted | Your card's foreign transaction fee and the conversion rate offered |

| Eligibility | Open to anyone or limited to residents | The rate conditions for any residency or ID requirement |

| Exact listing | Similar names, different properties or categories | Address, hotel name and the exact category you are booking |

## How to book a hotel from another country by hand

If you want to try it yourself, a careful process looks like this:

- **Fix the hotel and dates first**Changing either one resets everything you have checked.

- **Write down your baseline**The total price with taxes and fees, the cancellation terms and whether breakfast is included.

- **Go private and switch country**Open a private browser window, log out of booking accounts and connect a VPN to another country.

- **Search the same stay**Same hotel, dates and guests. Record the total, not the headline price.

- **Repeat**Try as many countries as you have patience for, and check local agencies where you can read the site.

- **Check conditions and fees before paying**Read the rate conditions for residency rules, and check whether your card charges a foreign transaction fee. Many cards do, commonly around 3 percent, which can cancel out a small saving. Decline the option to pay in your own currency at checkout if the conversion rate is poor.

- **Prefer refundable when the gap is small**That way you can rebook if a lower price appears later.

This works, but it does not scale. Each country takes minutes, VPN connections are sometimes blocked, and even a patient traveler stops after five or ten countries. There are 195. The practical limits are covered in [VPN vs. Arbitrica for hotel booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/vpn-vs-arbitrica-hotel-booking.html).

## Why searching from all 195 countries matters

Because the winning country moves with the hotel, the dates and the seller, the only reliable method is to check every country, every time. The lowest price is often in a country nobody would think to try.

> Chart: By hand, a VPN checks one country at a time. Arbitrica searches the same item from 195 countries at once.

That is what Arbitrica does. It is a personal AI agent that meets you at checkout when you are about to pay, searches the same hotel from 195 countries and finds the lowest price on Earth for it, at a different seller from the one you are on. It validates that the offer is for the identical hotel and that the total includes taxes and fees, checks that the price will not suddenly change, and then prepares the booking so you only review and pay. You can read the steps on [how it works](https://arbitrica.com/how-it-works.html).

In one real booking, a hotel was offered on Booking.com for $1,527.39. Arbitrica found the identical hotel for $1,180.27 and earned the user $347.12, about 23 percent. Results vary by hotel and date. Research showed that people earn on average $47 per hotel booking with Arbitrica, and up to $3,000 a year.

Prices also keep moving after you book. Arbitrica's approach repeats the search after purchase until the free cancellation window ends, so a lower price that appears later can still be used: a new booking is prepared at that price, and the original is cancelled only once the new booking is confirmed. The article on [hotel price drops after booking](https://arbitrica.com/blog/hotel-price-drop-after-booking.html) explains how that works. The same idea applies beyond hotels, to flights, event tickets and online shopping. Arbitrica also serves companies: teams traveling to trade shows and conferences, and the operations and travel managers who book for them.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which country is cheapest to book hotels from?

No single country is always cheapest. The lowest price for the same hotel depends on the hotel, the dates and which sellers are active in each country, so the winning country changes from booking to booking.

### Can I book a hotel from another country cheaper?

Often, yes. The same hotel is often 5 to 30 percent cheaper when booked from another country, because different countries get access to different inventory, sellers, local rates and promotions. Always compare the final total with taxes and fees.

### Does a VPN alone make hotels cheaper?

Not by itself. Changing your connection on the same site rarely moves the price of the same rate much. Savings come from the different offers and sellers available in other countries, and finding them by hand means checking many countries one at a time.

### Will the hotel honor a booking made from another country?

Yes, as long as the rate has no residency restriction. Read the rate conditions, because some local rates require proof of residence at check-in.
